definition_zh: 满不在乎；从容不迫；漫不经心
definition_en: a relaxed, unconcerned manner that suggests nothing can disturb it
core_image: 一个人在漏水的船上，先把杯子扶正，再慢慢讲起天气
scene: 火警响了，所有人都在找出口，他还在把咖啡喝完。 Her nonchalance convinced no one that she was calm.
sceneCN: 这里 nonchalance 指故作从容（第 1 个义项：看似毫不在意）；句意为她的满不在乎没能让任何人相信她真的镇定。

pos.zh: 满不在乎；从容不迫；漫不经心

senses.title: Apparent unconcern
senses.definition: a manner that shows no worry about what is happening
senses.definitionCN: 对正在发生的事不显露担忧的态度
senses.example: Her nonchalance convinced no one that she was calm.
senses.exampleCN: 她的满不在乎没能让任何人相信她真的镇定。
senses.why: The word describes the surface, and surfaces can be made: what looks careless may be carefully built.
senses.whyCN: 这个词描述表面，而表面是可以造出来的：看似无意，可能精心搭成。

senses.title: Calm under pressure
senses.definition: real ease of manner in a situation that would disturb most people
senses.definitionCN: 在多数人会被扰动的场合中真实的从容
senses.example: He met the bad news with the nonchalance of a man who had expected it.
senses.exampleCN: 他以预料之中的人才有的从容面对坏消息。
senses.why: Here the word is sincere: the ease is not performed but comes from having already absorbed the bad news.
senses.whyCN: 这里的词是真诚的：从容不是演出来的，而是因为早已消化了坏消息。

senses.title: Studied indifference
senses.definition: deliberately performed unconcern meant to be noticed
senses.definitionCN: 故意演出来、希望被注意到的漠不关心
senses.example: The nonchalance of his shrug was too quick to be real.
senses.exampleCN: 他那一耸肩的漠然太快，不像是真的。
senses.why: When indifference is performed, the performance itself gives the feeling away.
senses.whyCN: 当漠然被表演时，表演本身就泄露了情感。

senses.title: Nonchalance in dress
senses.definition: an easy, unforced style that refuses to try too hard
senses.definitionCN: 拒绝过度用力的轻松风格
senses.example: The room was furnished with expensive nonchalance.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间以昂贵的随意布置。
senses.why: The word extends from manners to style, because both can show an ease that costs effort to build.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从举止延伸到风格，因为两者都能显出需要费力才能搭出的轻松。

senses.title: Nonchalance as mask
senses.definition: unconcern used to hide fear, anger or interest
senses.definitionCN: 用来掩藏恐惧、愤怒或兴趣的漠然
senses.example: His nonchalance was a mask that slipped when her name came up.
senses.exampleCN: 他的淡然是一张面具，在她名字出现时滑落了。
senses.why: A mask is most visible at the moment it is needed most.
senses.whyCN: 面具在最需要它的时刻最显眼。

senses.title: Nonchalance in danger
senses.definition: a cool manner that steadies other people
senses.definitionCN: 使他人稳定的冷静态度
senses.example: The pilot's nonchalance kept the passengers from panicking.
senses.exampleCN: 飞行员的从容防止了乘客恐慌。
senses.why: In a crisis, manner is a public resource: one calm person can lend calm to many.
senses.whyCN: 危机中，态度是公共资源：一个镇定的人可以把镇定借给许多人。

senses.title: The nonchalance of wealth
senses.definition: the ease that comes from being able to afford mistakes
senses.definitionCN: 因为付得起错误代价而生的轻松
senses.example: The nonchalance of the collector annoyed the young artists.
senses.exampleCN: 这位收藏家的随意让年轻艺术家们恼火。
senses.why: Ease looks different depending on who can afford it, and the word can carry that criticism.
senses.whyCN: 轻松看起来不一样，取决于谁付得起，而这个词能带上这层批评。

senses.title: The cost of nonchalance
senses.definition: the harm done when unconcern is taken for competence
senses.definitionCN: 当漠然被当作能力时造成的损害
senses.example: His nonchalance about the deadline lost the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 他对截止日期的漫不经心弄丢了合同。
senses.why: The same manner that looks confident can also look careless, and only results separate them.
senses.whyCN: 同一种态度可以显得自信，也可以显得粗心，只有结果能把它们分开。

intro.en: Nonchalance joins not with a French verb meaning to be warm about something, so it means not heated.
intro.cn: nonchalance 把「不」与一个意为「对某事发热」的法语动词接在一起，意思就是「没有热起来」。

items.en: French nonchalance meant indifference, from non- and chaloir.
items.cn: 法语 nonchalance 意为漠不关心，由 non- 与 chaloir 构成。

items.en: Chaloir meant to be warm or concerned about something, from Latin calere.
items.cn: chaloir 意为对某事发热、挂心，出自拉丁语 calere。

items.en: Calere means to be warm, and gives calorie and caloric.
items.cn: calere 意为发热，给出 calorie 与 caloric。

items.en: English borrowed the noun in the 18c. as a word for fashionable ease.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪借入这个名词，指一种时髦的从容。

items.en: Modern English uses it for both genuine coolness and performed indifference.
items.cn: 现代英语用它指真实的冷静，也指表演出的漠然。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the warm root; the near-meaning group separates kinds of coolness.
note.cn: 形近组保留「热」的词根；近义组区分不同种类的冷静。

entries.definition: calmly unconcerned.
entries.definitionCN: 镇定而不在乎的。

entries.definition: in an unconcerned way.
entries.definitionCN: 以不在乎的方式。

entries.definition: old French for to care or be warm.
entries.definitionCN: 古法语「挂心、发热」。

entries.definition: a unit of heat or food energy.
entries.definitionCN: 热量或食物能量单位。

entries.definition: lack of interest or concern.
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏兴趣或关心。

entries.definition: calm control of one's feelings and face.
entries.definitionCN: 对情感与表情的镇定掌控。

entries.definition: assurance that does not wobble under pressure.
entries.definitionCN: 压力下不摇晃的自信。

entries.definition: cheerful lack of worry.
entries.definitionCN: 愉快的无忧无虑。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of someone righting a cup on a leaking boat before mentioning the weather.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想留住「船在漏水，某人先把杯子扶正，再谈起天气」的画面。

normal.en: Nonchalance = non + chaloir, not warm about it.
normal.cn: nonchalance = non + chaloir，对它不发热。

normal.en: The chaloir part hides in calorie: warmth is heat.
normal.cn: chaloir 藏在 calorie 里：暖就是热。

normal.en: Think of a shrug performed exactly one beat too fast.
normal.cn: 想象一次快了半拍的耸肩。

normal.en: Say non-shuh-LAHNS; the soft ending sounds like a dismissal.
normal.cn: 读成 non-shuh-LAHNS，轻柔的结尾像一次打发。

normal.en: Pair it with composure: composure is real, nonchalance may be a surface.
normal.cn: 和 composure 配对：composure 是真的，nonchalance 可能是表面。

abstract.en: Indifference can be strength or theatre, and the difference is usually timing.
abstract.cn: 漠然可以是力量，也可以是戏，而差别通常在时机。

abstract.en: Calm in a crisis is a gift to everyone standing nearby.
abstract.cn: 危机中的镇定是给身边所有人的礼物。

abstract.en: Ease that costs nothing to the person showing it may cost others a great deal.
abstract.cn: 对展示者毫无代价的轻松，可能让别人付出很多。

examples.en: Her nonchalance convinced no one that she was calm.
examples.cn: 她的满不在乎没能让任何人相信她真的镇定。

examples.en: The pilot's nonchalance kept the passengers from panicking.
examples.cn: 飞行员的从容防止了乘客恐慌。

examples.en: His nonchalance about the deadline lost the contract.
examples.cn: 他对截止日期的漫不经心弄丢了合同。

dict_mnemonic.text: non（不）+ chaloir（发热、挂心）：不发热，就是「满不在乎」。

root: 法语 nonchalance，源自 non-（不）与 chaloir（发热、挂心），再上溯拉丁语 calere

sensesIntro.en: Nonchalance is coolness of surface; the senses differ in whether the coolness is real, performed, useful or costly.
sensesIntro.cn: nonchalance 是表面的冷；各义项的差别在于这份冷是真的、演的、有用的，还是代价高的。

core.en: A SURFACE THAT DOES NOT HEAT UP
core.cn: 不升温的表面

branches.en: The surface, the performance and the mask.
branches.cn: 表面、表演与面具。

branches.en: Real calm that steady others in danger.
branches.cn: 在危险中稳住他人的真实镇定。

branches.en: Style and the ease that money can buy.
branches.cn: 风格，以及金钱能买到的轻松。

branches.en: The failure when ease is mistaken for competence.
branches.cn: 轻松被误认作能力时的失败。

branches.en: Timing and result decide whether it reads as strength or carelessness.
branches.cn: 时机与结果决定它读作力量还是粗心。

intro.en: The chal family is about heat: nonchalance has none, calorie measures it, and caloric describes it.
intro.cn: chal 词族与热有关：nonchalance 没有热，calorie 衡量热，caloric 描述热。

latinIntro.en: Latin calere means to be warm; French turned it into caring, and non- turned caring into coolness.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 calere 意为发热；法语把它变成「挂心」，而 non- 把挂心变成冷淡。

items.meaning: a state of not being warm

items.exampleCN: 他漫不经心地挥了挥手。
她漫不经心地读了裁决。

definition_zh: 迁移；移居；迁徙；移民潮；数据迁移；细胞迁移；污染物迁移；劳动力流动；系统间转移
definition_en: the movement of people, animals or other things from one place, region or system to another, especially over a long distance or in large numbers
core_image: 暮色中一群鸟排成人字，从一片湿地飞向另一片湿地
scene: 这里指「迁移」。 At dusk the birds form a wedge and leave one marsh for another: their movement is migration.
sceneCN: 这里 migration 是「迁徙」（第 2 个义项：动物迁徙）；句意：暮色中鸟群排成人字，离开一片湿地飞向另一片湿地，它们的移动就是迁徙。图中可辨识物件：人字形鸟群、起飞的湿地、远处的湿地、暮色天空、芦苇。

pos.zh: 迁移；移居；迁徙；移民潮；数据迁移

forms.label: 单数（一次迁移或迁移这件事）
复数（多批迁移或多条迁徙路线）

senses.title: People moving to a new place to live
senses.titleCN: 人的迁移：搬到另一处生活
senses.definition: the movement of people from one place or country to another in order to settle there
senses.definitionCN: 人们从一个地方或国家移到另一个地方或国家定居
senses.example: Migration from the countryside to the cities changed the labour market.
senses.exampleCN: 从乡村向城市的迁移改变了劳动力市场。
senses.why: Latin migrare means to move from one place to another, and migratio names that moving. Applied to people, the change of place becomes a change of home.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 migrare 意为从一处移到另一处，migratio 指这一移动。用在人身上，换地方就变成了换家。

senses.title: Animal migration: seasonal movement between regions
senses.titleCN: 动物迁徙：随季节在区域间移动
senses.definition: the seasonal movement of animals, birds or fish from one region to another and often back again
senses.definitionCN: 动物、鸟类或鱼类随季节从一个地区移到另一地区，且常常再返回
senses.example: The migration of the geese follows the river valley every autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 每年秋天雁群的迁徙都沿着河谷走。
senses.why: The same verb fits animals because they also leave one place for another. The word adds nothing about distance; the round trip and the season are supplied by context.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词也适用于动物，因为它们同样离开一处去另一处。词本身不涉及距离；往返与季节是由语境提供的。

senses.title: A wave of movement: numbers on the move
senses.definition: a large-scale movement of people or animals considered as a quantity or a trend
senses.definitionCN: 被当作数量或趋势来看待的大规模人潮或兽群移动
senses.example: The century saw a migration of millions across the border.
senses.exampleCN: 那个世纪有数百万人越过边境迁移。
senses.why: Once many journeys are counted together, migration stops being one person's move and becomes a demographic event, measured and graphed by agencies.
senses.whyCN: 当许多趟行程被一起计数，migration 就不再是一个人的搬家，而成为一个人口事件，被机构测量并绘成图表。

senses.title: Data migration: moving information between systems
senses.titleCN: 数据迁移：把信息搬到另一套系统
senses.definition: the transfer of data from one storage system, format or platform to another
senses.definitionCN: 把数据从一种存储系统、格式或平台转移到另一种
senses.example: The data migration took three nights and two rollbacks.
senses.exampleCN: 这次数据迁移用了三个夜晚和两次回滚。
senses.why: Computing keeps the literal image: records that lived in one place are moved to another. The risk is the same as in any move, that something is lost on the way.
senses.whyCN: 计算机领域保留了字面意象：原本住在一处的记录被搬到另一处。风险也跟任何搬家一样：路上可能丢东西。

senses.title: Cell migration: cells moving through tissue
senses.titleCN: 细胞迁移：细胞在组织中移动
senses.definition: in biology, the directed movement of cells through tissue, as in wound healing or development
senses.definitionCN: 生物学中指细胞在组织中定向移动，如伤口愈合或发育过程中的移动
senses.example: Cell migration is central to how wounds close.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞迁移是伤口如何闭合的核心环节。
senses.why: Biology applies the word at a scale invisible to the eye. A cell leaves one position for another, so the same migrare serves, with the 'journey' compressed to micrometres.
senses.whyCN: 生物学把这个词用在肉眼不可见的尺度。细胞离开一个位置去另一个位置，所以同一个 migrare 仍然适用，只是「行程」被压缩到微米级。

senses.title: Pollutant migration: spreading through soil and water
senses.titleCN: 污染物迁移：在土壤与水中扩散
senses.definition: the movement of a substance, especially a pollutant, through soil, water or air
senses.definitionCN: 物质、尤指污染物在土壤、水或空气中的移动
senses.example: The study traced the migration of nitrates into the groundwater.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究追踪了硝酸盐向地下水的迁移。
senses.why: Here the mover is not a creature but a substance. The word still means a change of place, and the scientific use adds the question of how far and how fast.
senses.whyCN: 这里移动的不是生物，而是物质。词仍指换地方，科学用法则再加上「多远、多快」的问题。

senses.title: Labour migration: workers following demand
senses.titleCN: 劳动力迁移：工人跟着需求走
senses.definition: the movement of workers between regions or countries in search of employment
senses.definitionCN: 工人为寻找就业而在地区或国家之间移动
senses.example: Seasonal labour migration fills the harvest with hands.
senses.exampleCN: 季节性劳动力迁移为收割季节补足了人手。
senses.why: When the reason for moving is work, the word becomes an economic term. The same journey is now explained by wages rather than by home.
senses.whyCN: 当移动的原因是工作时，这个词就成了经济术语。同一趟行程，如今用工资来解释，而不是用家。

senses.title: Any transfer between systems
senses.titleCN: 一般迁移：在一个系统与另一个系统之间转移
senses.definition: a general transfer from one system, category or state to another
senses.definitionCN: 从一种系统、类别或状态转移到另一种的统称
senses.example: The migration of files from paper archives to digital ones took a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 把档案从纸质迁到数字形式用了一个年代。
senses.why: The general sense is simply 'a move from one container to another'. It keeps the word usable for archives, accounts, populations and species alike.
senses.whyCN: 一般义就是「从一个容器搬到另一个容器」。这使这个词能用于档案、账户、人口与物种。

intro.en: Migration comes from Latin migratio, the noun of migrare 'to move from one place to another'. English borrowed it in the 17th century, at first for the movement of people, and extended it to animals, cells and data in later centuries. The deeper link to a root meaning 'to change' is generally accepted but not certain. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: migration 出自拉丁语 migratio，即 migrare「从一处移到另一处」的名词。英语在 17 世纪借入，最初指人的迁移，后来几个世纪才扩展到动物、细胞与数据。它与一个意为「改变」的词根有更深联系，这一点一般认为成立，但并非确证。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Data migration and cell migration become standard phrases as computing and cell biology grow.
items.cn: 随着计算技术与细胞生物学的发展，data migration（数据迁移）与 cell migration（细胞迁移）成为固定说法。

items.en: The study of bird migration gives the word its popular natural-history sense.
items.cn: 对鸟类迁徙的研究赋予这个词流行的自然史含义。

items.en: English migration is recorded, naming the movement of people from one country or region to another.
items.cn: 英语 migration 见于记载，指人从一个国家或地区迁往另一个。

items.en: migratio is the noun of migrare; the same verb gives migrate, migrant, immigrate and emigrate.
items.cn: migratio 是 migrare 的名词；同一个动词给出 migrate、migrant、immigrate、emigrate。

items.en: A reconstructed root *mei- 'to change, go' is often proposed behind migrare, though the connection is generally accepted rather than proven.
items.cn: 常有人为 migrare 提出重构词根 *mei-「改变、行走」，但这一联系一般认为成立，而非已证明。

note.en: The first group separates the two prefixed relatives and one false friend; the second compares words for movement that differ in scale or cause.
note.cn: 第一组把两个带前缀的同族词和一个假朋友分开；第二组比较规模或成因不同的移动类词。

entries.definition: the act of leaving one's own country to settle elsewhere. The prefix e- 'out' fixes the point of view at the country of departure.
entries.definitionCN: 离开本国到别处定居的行为。前缀 e-「向外」把视角固定在出发国。

entries.definition: the act of coming into a country to settle. The prefix im- 'in' fixes the point of view at the receiving country, so the same journey is emigration or immigration depending on who is counting.
entries.definitionCN: 进入某国定居的行为。前缀 im-「向内」把视角固定在接收国，因此同一趟行程，看谁在计数，就或叫移出或叫移入。

entries.definition: a severe recurring headache. It comes through French from Greek hēmikrania 'half the skull', and has nothing to do with migrare despite the shared opening.
entries.definitionCN: 反复发作的剧烈头痛。它经法语来自希腊语 hēmikrania「半个头骨」，虽开头相同，却与 migrare 无关。

entries.definition: any change of position. It is the widest word, with no implication of settling, season or distance.
entries.definitionCN: 任何位置变化。它是最宽泛的词，不含定居、季节或距离的意味。

entries.definition: the act of moving a person, company or object to a new place. It is usually a single planned move, where migration suggests many moves or a recurring pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 把个人、公司或物件搬到新地点。它通常指一次有计划的搬迁，而 migration 暗示许多次移动或反复出现的模式。

entries.definition: the forcing of people from their homes by war, disaster or development. It stresses that the move was compelled, not chosen.
entries.definitionCN: 因战争、灾害或开发而被迫离开家园。它强调移动是被迫而非自愿。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real pieces of the word and its real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想只使用这个词真实的构成成分和真实同族词，不用编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: migrare means 'to move from one place to another'; every sense is that verb wearing a different subject.
normal.cn: migrare 意为「从一处移到另一处」；每个义项都是这个动词换了个主语。

normal.en: e- 'out' and im- 'in' split the family: emigration looks from the leaving side, immigration from the arriving side.
normal.cn: e-「向外」与 im-「向内」把这个词族分开：emigration 从离开方看，immigration 从到达方看。

normal.en: Migraine is not a relative: its Greek source means 'half the skull', not 'moving away'.
normal.cn: migraine 不是同族词：它的希腊来源意为「半个头骨」，而不是「迁走」。

normal.en: The -tion ending names the event, while migrant names the person who performs it.
normal.cn: -tion 词尾命名事件，而 migrant 命名实施这一行为的人。

normal.en: Data and cells migrate in the same grammatical way as birds: something leaves one place for another.
normal.cn: 数据与细胞的「迁移」在语法上和鸟一样：某物离开一处去另一处。

abstract.en: Picture a dotted line from one marsh to another, followed each year by a new generation.
abstract.cn: 想象一条从这片湿地连到那片湿地的虚线，每年由新一代沿着它飞。

abstract.en: Any migration has three parts: a place left, a route, and a place arrived at; every sense uses those three.
abstract.cn: 任何迁移都有三部分：离开的地方、路线、抵达的地方；每个义项都用到这三样。

abstract.en: The word never asks whether the move was good, only that it happened and in which direction.
abstract.cn: 这个词从不过问迁移好不好，只问它是否发生、朝哪个方向。

examples.en: Rural migration has emptied many mountain villages.
examples.cn: 乡村人口外迁让许多山村空了。

examples.en: The migration of monarch butterflies covers thousands of kilometres.
examples.cn: 帝王蝶的迁徙要跨越数千公里。

examples.en: The company scheduled the data migration for a weekend.
examples.cn: 公司把数据迁移安排在周末。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「买个雷神」——候鸟一路买个雷神当路标，年年迁往同一处 → migration 迁徙、迁移

root: 拉丁语 migrare「从一处移到另一处」→ migratio → 英语 migration。核心是「离开一处、沿路、抵达另一处」，主语可以是人、鸟、细胞、数据或污染物。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses keep one image: a dotted line from one place to another. What changes is who or what travels along it — settlers, birds, whole populations, records, cells, dissolved chemicals, workers, or any transferable thing.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都保留同一个意象：从一处连到另一处的一条虚线。变化的只是沿这条线走的是什么——定居者、鸟、整批人口、记录、细胞、溶解的化学物质、工人，或任何可转移之物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: at dusk a wedge of birds leaves one marsh for another.
core.cn: 核心意象：暮色中一群鸟排成人字，离开一片湿地飞向另一片。

branches.en: PEOPLE MOVING: settlers change home, and workers change region in search of wages.
branches.cn: 人的移动：定居者换了家，工人为工资换了地区。

branches.en: ANIMALS MOVING: the same route is flown or walked each season, often back and forth.
branches.cn: 动物的移动：同一路线每个季节被飞过或走过，常常来回。

branches.en: THE WAVE: many journeys counted together become a demographic or ecological trend.
branches.cn: 浪潮：许多趟行程合并计数，就成为人口或生态趋势。

branches.en: INVISIBLE MOVERS: records leave one system, cells leave one position, both by the same literal image.
branches.cn: 看不见的移动者：记录离开一套系统，细胞离开一个位置，两者用的是同一个字面意象。

branches.en: SUBSTANCES AND TRANSFERS: pollutants travel through soil and water, and any item can be moved between containers.
branches.cn: 物质与转移：污染物穿过土壤与水，任何东西都可以从一个容器搬到另一个。

intro.en: Migration is Latin migr- plus -ation. The ending -ation names an action; the stem migr- comes from migrare 'to move from one place to another', and the prefixes e- and im- decide the direction of the move.
intro.cn: migration 是拉丁词干 migr- 加 -ation。词尾 -ation 命名动作；词干 migr- 来自 migrare「从一处移到另一处」，而前缀 e- 与 im- 决定移动的方向。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb is migrare 'to move, change place'. Its family splits by prefix: e- 'out' gives emigrate, im- 'in' gives immigrate, and trans- 'across' gives transmigrate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁动词是 migrare「移动、换地方」。其词族按前缀分流：e-「向外」给出 emigrate，im-「向内」给出 immigrate，trans-「穿过」给出 transmigrate。

items.meaning: the act of moving from one place to another
items.meaningCN: 迁移；迁徙（-ation 构成动作名词）

items.meaning: to move from one region or system to another
items.example: Many birds migrate along this coast.
items.exampleCN: 许多鸟沿着这条海岸迁徙。

items.meaning: a person or animal that migrates
items.exampleCN: 这个营地安置着外来务工人员。

items.meaning: given to migrating, or relating to migration
to leave one's country to settle elsewhere
items.meaningCN: 移出本国；迁往外地（e- 表示向外）
items.exampleCN: 她家在 1980 年代移居国外。

items.meaning: the act of leaving a country
items.example: Emigration drained the island of young workers.
items.exampleCN: 人口外迁让这座岛失去了年轻劳力。

items.meaning: to come into a country to settle
items.meaningCN: 移入；移民入境（im- 表示向内）
items.exampleCN: 他们带着三个孩子移居入境。

items.meaning: the act of entering a country to settle
a passage across, or the passing of a soul into another body
items.meaningCN: 横越迁移；灵魂转世（trans- 表示穿过）
items.example: The old doctrine taught the transmigration of souls.
items.exampleCN: 这一古老教义讲灵魂的转世。

items.structure: the same adjective used in medicine for pain that moves
items.meaning: of symptoms that shift from one part to another
items.meaningCN: （医学）游走性的：症状从一处移到另一处
items.example: The patient reported migratory joint pain.
items.exampleCN: 病人诉称有关节游走性疼痛。

latinEntries.meaning: forms a noun of action or result
latinEntries.meaningCN: 构成表示动作或结果的名词

definition_zh: 苦行的；禁欲的；清心寡欲的；苦行者
definition_en: practicing strict self-denial and simple living, or a person who does so
core_image: 山洞里的苦行者：一张草席、一件粗衣、拒绝一切享乐
scene: 他放弃高薪工作，搬进山中木屋，每天只吃一餐、睡四小时。 The monk lived an ascetic life of prayer, fasting, and silence.
sceneCN: 这里 ascetic 是「苦行的、禁欲的」（第 1 个义项：自我克制的生活方式）；句意是僧侣过着祈祷、斋戒与静默的苦修生活。

pos.zh: 苦行的；禁欲的
苦行者；禁欲者

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「苦行；禁欲主义」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「苦行地；清苦地」
希腊语同源词，义为「训练；修习」

senses.title: Self-denying in lifestyle
senses.definition: living simply and strictly, avoiding pleasures and comforts
senses.definitionCN: 生活简朴严格，回避享乐与舒适
senses.example: He kept an ascetic diet of rice, vegetables, and water.
senses.exampleCN: 他坚持米饭、蔬菜和清水的苦行饮食。
senses.why: Greek askesis meant training; just as athletes train hard, ascetics train the soul by refusing comfort.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 askesis 意为训练；正如运动员苦练，苦行者以拒绝舒适来锻炼灵魂。

senses.title: Severe and bare in style
senses.definition: plain and severe in appearance or atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 外表或氛围上朴素、严苛、毫无装饰
senses.example: The room had an ascetic beauty: white walls, a bare table, one chair.
senses.exampleCN: 房间有一种清苦之美：白墙、空桌、一把椅子。
senses.why: Denying comfort extends to design, where nothing decorative survives.
senses.whyCN: 对舒适的克制延伸到设计上，任何装饰都无法留存。

senses.title: A person practicing self-denial
senses.definition: one who renounces material comforts for spiritual discipline
senses.definitionCN: 为精神修习而放弃物质享受的人
senses.example: Desert ascetics were visited by pilgrims seeking wisdom.
senses.exampleCN: 朝圣者纷纷拜访沙漠中的苦行者，寻求智慧。
senses.why: When the adjective names a way of life, it also names the people who live it.
senses.whyCN: 当形容词指一种生活方式时，也指践行这种生活的人。

intro.en: Ascetic comes from Greek asketes, one who trains, from askein to exercise or train, first said of athletes.
intro.cn: ascetic 源自希腊语 askētēs（训练者），来自 askein（操练），最初形容运动员。

items.en: Askein meant to work raw material, then to train the body.
items.cn: 希腊语 askein 本指加工原料，后指训练身体。

items.en: Asketes named an athlete or one in training.
items.cn: askētēs 指运动员或受训者。

items.en: Christians applied the word to spiritual athletes, those training the soul.
items.cn: 希腊化时期基督徒把该词用于「灵魂的运动员」，即修行者。

items.en: Late Latin asceta meant a monk.
items.cn: 后期拉丁语 asceta 指僧侣。

items.en: English borrowed ascetic in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语借入 ascetic。

note.en: Ascetic describes chosen discipline, not poverty imposed from outside.
note.cn: ascetic 指主动选择的克己，而不是外界强加的贫困。

entries.definition: the doctrine or practice of self-denial
entries.definitionCN: 苦行主义；禁欲主义

entries.definition: relating to beauty, a different root entirely
entries.definitionCN: 审美的；美学的（拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: in an ascetic manner
entries.definitionCN: 苦行地；清苦地

entries.definition: Greek source word meaning one in training
entries.definitionCN: 希腊语源词，指受训者

entries.definition: of athletes, the original comparison for ascetics
entries.definitionCN: 运动的；运动员的（与苦行者本义相对照）

entries.definition: severe and plain, without comfort or luxury
entries.definitionCN: 严峻朴素的；清苦的

entries.definition: refusing one's own pleasures
entries.definitionCN: 克己的；自我否定的

entries.definition: like the life of a monastery
entries.definitionCN: 僧侣的；修道院式的

entries.definition: sparing and economical
entries.definitionCN: 节俭的

entries.definition: enduring hardship without complaint
entries.definitionCN: 坚忍的；禁欲的

normalIntro.en: Hear ask- inside ascetic: an ascetic asks nothing of comfort.
normalIntro.cn: 在 ascetic 里听出 ask（求）：苦行者对享乐「一无所求」。

normal.en: Greek askein: to train like an athlete.
normal.cn: 希腊语 askein：像运动员一样训练。

normal.en: ascetics are spiritual athletes.
normal.cn: 苦行者是「灵魂的运动员」。

normal.en: do not mix with aesthetic, about beauty.
normal.cn: 勿与 aesthetic（审美的）混淆。

normal.en: asceticism names the whole practice.
normal.cn: asceticism 指整套苦修实践。

normal.en: austerities are the deeds of an ascetic.
normal.cn: austerities 是苦行者的具体行为。

abstract.en: Picture a stone cell with one small window.
abstract.cn: 想象一间只有一个窄窗的石屋。

abstract.en: Feel the cold morning water of a ritual wash.
abstract.cn: 感受清晨仪式用水的冰冷。

abstract.en: See the athlete at dawn, training the soul instead of the body.
abstract.cn: 看见黎明训练的运动员——练的是灵魂而非身体。

examples.en: The founder lived an ascetic life until his death.
examples.cn: 创始人一生过着苦行的生活。

examples.en: Her ascetic apartment held only a mattress and books.
examples.cn: 她清苦的公寓里只有一张床垫和书。

examples.en: Ancient ascetics withdrew to the desert to pray.
examples.cn: 古代苦行者隐居沙漠祈祷。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「饿塞体」——饿着肚子、塞住欲望、修成身体之苦，正如 ascetic 的禁欲修行。

root: 源自希腊语 askein（操练、修习）与 askētēs（训练者），本用于运动员，后被基督教用于修行者。

sensesIntro.en: The athlete's training image moves from bodily discipline to spiritual denial to bare aesthetics.
sensesIntro.cn: 运动员训练的意象从身体的自律移向灵魂的克己，再到朴素无饰的风格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an athlete of the soul training by refusing comfort
core.cn: 核心意象：以拒绝舒适来训练的灵魂运动员

branches.en: strict self-denial in daily life
branches.cn: 日常生活中的严格克己

branches.en: bare, undecorated severity
branches.cn: 朴素无饰的严峻

branches.en: the person who renounces comfort
branches.cn: 放弃舒适的修行者

branches.en: discipline chosen for spirit
branches.cn: 为精神而选择的自律

branches.en: the visible mark of renunciation
branches.cn: 克己的外在印记

intro.en: The Greek askein family is small in English but carries the key idea of disciplined practice.
intro.cn: 希腊语 askein 词族在英语中虽小，却承载「修习」这一关键概念。

latinIntro.en: This is a Greek, not Latin, family; there are no Latin cognates in English.
latinIntro.cn: 这是希腊语词族而非拉丁语词族，英语中没有拉丁同源词。

items.meaning: one who lives in the wilderness

definition_zh: 半球；地球半球；大脑半球；半球图；（活动）范围
definition_en: one half of a sphere, especially the northern or southern half of the earth
core_image: 一个球被过球心的大圆切成两半，每一半都保留着完整的弧面
scene: 地理老师在球体模型上沿赤道画了一圈。 The teacher cuts the globe along the equator to show each hemisphere.
sceneCN: 这里 hemisphere 指「地球被赤道分成的南北两半之一」（第 1 个义项：以赤道为界划分的地球半球）；句意为老师沿赤道切开地球仪，展示南北两个半球。图中可辨识物件：地球仪、赤道线、半圆剖面、支架。

pos.zh: 半球；地球的南北半球
大脑半球；（活动）范围

senses.title: Half of the earth
senses.titleCN: 地球的半球：以赤道或经圈分成的两半
senses.definition: either the northern or southern half of the earth, divided by the equator, or the eastern and western halves divided by meridians
senses.definitionCN: 地球被赤道分成南北两半，或被经线分成东西两半的任一半
senses.example: Most of the world's population lives in the northern hemisphere.
senses.exampleCN: 世界人口大部分住在北半球。
senses.why: Hemi- 'half' plus sphaira 'sphere' literally gives 'half ball'; once applied to the earth, it names each of its two halves.
senses.whyCN: hemi-「一半」加 sphaira「球」字面就是「半个球」；用于地球后，就指地球的两半之一。

senses.title: Half of any sphere
senses.titleCN: 半球体：任意球体被大圆切开的一半
senses.definition: one of the two halves of a sphere cut by a plane through its centre
senses.definitionCN: 球体被过球心平面切开后的任一半
senses.example: A hemisphere has a curved surface and one flat circular face.
senses.exampleCN: 半球有一个曲面和一个平的圆面。
senses.why: The geometry sense is the literal one: a sphere divided by a great circle leaves two equal halves.
senses.whyCN: 几何义是字面义：球被大圆分割，留下两个相等的半。

senses.title: One side of the brain
senses.titleCN: 大脑半球：大脑左右两半之一
senses.definition: either of the two halves of the brain, left and right, divided by the central fissure
senses.definitionCN: 大脑被中央沟分成左右两半的任一半
senses.example: The left hemisphere usually handles language in right-handed people.
senses.exampleCN: 惯用右手的人通常由左半球处理语言。
senses.why: The brain is roughly spherical, so its two lobes were named hemispheres when anatomy borrowed the word.
senses.whyCN: 大脑近似球形，解剖学借这个词时就把左右两叶称作半球。

senses.title: A map of one half of the globe
senses.titleCN: 半球图：展示地球一半的地图
senses.definition: a map projection that shows one half of the globe at a time
senses.definitionCN: 一次展示地球一半的地图投影
senses.example: The atlas opens with a hemisphere map of the Pacific.
senses.exampleCN: 这本图集以一幅太平洋半球图开篇。
senses.why: A flat map can show only half the globe without severe distortion, so such maps are called hemisphere maps.
senses.whyCN: 平面地图不严重变形时只能展示地球一半，这类图因而叫半球图。

senses.title: Eastern or western division
senses.titleCN: 东西半球：按经度划分的政治地理分区
senses.definition: either of the two east-west divisions of the globe, often used as a cultural or political label
senses.definitionCN: 地球按经度划分的东西两半，常用作文化或政治标签
senses.example: The convention placed the new nation in the western hemisphere.
senses.exampleCN: 这一惯例把新国家归入西半球。
senses.why: Meridians can split the globe into two named halves just as the equator does, and those names then acquire cultural and political weight.
senses.whyCN: 经线也能像赤道一样把地球分成两个有名称的半，而这些名称随后带上文化与政治分量。

senses.title: Half of the celestial sphere
senses.titleCN: 天球半球：天球被地平圈分成的一半
senses.definition: either half of the sky as divided by the horizon or by a celestial great circle
senses.definitionCN: 天空被地平圈或天球大圆分成的任一半
senses.example: Astronomers chart the visible hemisphere before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 天文学家在黎明前绘制可见天球半球。
senses.why: The horizon cuts the spherical sky into a visible half and a hidden half, the same geometry as the globe.
senses.whyCN: 地平圈把球形天空切成可见与不可见两半，与地球的几何分割相同。

senses.title: A sphere of activity or influence
senses.titleCN: 活动范围：影响所及的领域（书面）
senses.definition: an area of activity, knowledge or influence, used figuratively
senses.definitionCN: 活动、知识或影响所及的范围，用于比喻
senses.example: The reform moved education into a different hemisphere of public debate.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革把教育推入公共讨论的另一个领域。
senses.why: The globe's two halves are imagined as two separate worlds, so any divided field can be called a hemisphere.
senses.whyCN: 地球的两半被想象成两个分开的世界，因此任何被分割的领域都可称为一个 hemisphere。

senses.title: Land or water hemisphere
senses.titleCN: 陆半球或水半球：按海陆分布划分的半球
senses.definition: either of two halves of the earth chosen to contain most of its land or most of its water
senses.definitionCN: 地球按陆地或水域最集中而划分出的两半之一
senses.example: The land hemisphere is centred near southern Europe.
senses.exampleCN: 陆半球以欧洲南部附近为中心。
senses.why: Geographers may choose the centre so that most land falls in one half and most water in the other, which makes the division a deliberate cut.
senses.whyCN: 地理学家可以选择中心，使大部分陆地落在一半、大部分水域落在另一半，因此这种划分是有意选定的切法。

intro.en: Hemisphere goes back to Greek hemisphairion, 'half a sphere', from hemi- 'half' and sphaira 'ball'. Latin took it as hemisphaerium and English borrowed it in the sixteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: hemisphere 上溯到希腊 hemisphairion「半个球」，由 hemi-「一半」与 sphaira「球」构成；拉丁作 hemisphaerium，英语在 16 世纪借入。年代均为约数。

items.en: Hemi- meant 'half' and is a productive prefix in English, as in hemicycle and hemisphere.
items.cn: hemi- 意为「一半」，在英语中是能产前缀，如 hemicycle 与 hemisphere。

items.en: Sphaira meant 'ball, globe'. Its deeper origin is not established; any Indo-European root proposed for it is a reconstruction, not a recorded form.
items.cn: sphaira 意为「球、globus」；其更深来源未得到证明，为其提出的任何印欧词根都属重构形式，而非有记录的词。

items.en: Hemi- plus sphaira gave hemisphairion, 'a half sphere', used by Greek geographers and astronomers.
items.cn: hemi- 加 sphaira 构成 hemisphairion「半球」，为希腊地理学家与天文学家所用。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek compound as hemisphaerium, keeping both elements intact.
items.cn: 拉丁把这个希腊复合词借作 hemisphaerium，两个成分原样保留。

items.en: English hemisphere appears in the sixteenth century, first for the halves of the celestial and terrestrial spheres.
items.cn: 英语 hemisphere 出现于 16 世纪，最初指天球与地球的半球。

items.en: The anatomical use for the two halves of the brain developed later; its exact first English date is uncertain, while the compound itself is transparent.
items.cn: 指大脑两半的解剖用法较晚出现；其英语首见确切年代不确定，但复合词本身结构透明。

note.en: Group one holds the -sphere words that look alike; group two holds words for halves, globes and brain regions.
note.cn: 第一组是外形相近的 -sphere 词；第二组是表示一半、球体与脑区的词。

entries.definition: From Greek atmos 'vapour' plus sphaira: the envelope of air around a planet, not a half of it.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 atmos「蒸汽」加 sphaira：行星周围的空气层，不是球的一半。

entries.definition: From Greek bios 'life' plus sphaira: the zone of living things, named by analogy with atmosphere.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 bios「生命」加 sphaira：生物所在圈层，仿 atmosphere 造出。

entries.definition: The ionised layer of the upper atmosphere; again a full shell, not a hemisphere.
entries.definitionCN: 高层大气中的电离层；同样是完整壳层而非半球。

entries.definition: From Latin stratum 'layer' plus sphaira: a layer of the atmosphere, with no half division.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 stratum「层」加 sphaira：大气的一层，不含对半分割。

entries.definition: The everyday word for one of two equal parts; hemisphere adds the spherical shape.
entries.definitionCN: 表示两个相等部分之一的日常词；hemisphere 另带球体形状。

entries.definition: The whole spherical earth or a model of it; a hemisphere is only one of its halves.
entries.definitionCN: 整个球形地球或其模型；半球只是它的一半。

entries.definition: A rounded projecting part, as of the brain or lung; hemisphere stresses the left-right division.
entries.definitionCN: 圆形突出的部分，如脑叶或肺叶；hemisphere 强调左右分半。

entries.definition: A band or region defined by climate or function; it cuts the globe into belts rather than halves.
entries.definitionCN: 按气候或功能划分的带或区域；它把地球切成带而非两半。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek compound, real map terms and real anatomy, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊复合词、真实的地图术语与真实的解剖学，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Hemi- 'half' + sphaira 'sphere': literally half a ball, then half the earth.
normal.cn: hemi-「一半」+ sphaira「球」：字面是半个球，再指地球的一半。

normal.en: The -sphere family (atmosphere, biosphere, ionosphere) is built on the same Greek 'ball'.
normal.cn: atmosphere、biosphere、ionosphere 等 -sphere 词族都建立在同一个希腊「球」上。

normal.en: Northern and southern hemispheres are divided by the equator; eastern and western by meridians.
normal.cn: 南北半球由赤道分开，东西半球由经线分开。

normal.en: The brain's two hemispheres are linked by the corpus callosum.
normal.cn: 大脑两个半球由胼胝体相连。

normal.en: A hemisphere map shows half the globe at once, which limits distortion.
normal.cn: 半球图一次展示地球一半，从而限制变形。

abstract.en: Picture an orange sliced exactly through its centre into two equal cups.
abstract.cn: 想象一只橙子沿正中心切成两只相等的杯状半。

abstract.en: Picture a theatre with the audience seated on one side of the stage only.
abstract.cn: 想象一座剧场，观众只坐在舞台的一侧。

abstract.en: Picture a conversation that belongs to one half of a divided family.
abstract.cn: 想象一场只属于分裂家庭中某一方的对话。

examples.en: Summer begins in the southern hemisphere in December.
examples.cn: 南半球的夏天在十二月开始。

examples.en: Each hemisphere of the brain has different functions.
examples.cn: 大脑每个半球各有不同功能。

examples.en: The map folds out into two hemispheres.
examples.cn: 这张地图展开后分成两个半球图。

dict_mnemonic.text: hemi（一半，如 hemi- 前缀）+ sphere（球）→ 半个球 → 半球、大脑半球

root: 希腊 hemisphairion「半球」= hemi-（一半）+ sphaira（球）；拉丁 hemisphaerium，英语 16 世纪借入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all begin with a sphere and a cut through its centre: the earth's halves, any ball's halves, the brain's two sides, a map of one half, the east-west labels, the sky's halves, a figurative field, and the land-water division.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从「球体被过球心切开」开始：地球两半、任意球体的两半、大脑两侧、展示一半的地图、东西半球标签、天空两半、比喻的领域，以及陆半球与水半球。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sphere cut exactly through its centre, leaving two equal curved halves.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个球被过球心切开，留下两个相等的弧面半。

branches.en: GEOMETRY TO EARTH: the literal half ball becomes the earth's northern and southern halves.
branches.cn: 几何到地球：字面的半个球变成地球的南北两半。

branches.en: BODY: the brain's two sides borrow the spherical division.
branches.cn: 身体：大脑两侧借用了球体的分割。

branches.en: DRAWN AND CHOSEN: maps show one half at a time, and land or water can define an uneven half.
branches.cn: 画出与选定：地图一次展示一半，陆地或水域也能划出不完全对等的一半。

branches.en: LABEL AND METAPHOR: east-west halves are political names, and any field can be pictured as a half.
branches.cn: 标签与比喻：东西半球是政治名称，任何领域也可被想象成一半。

branches.en: SKY: the celestial sphere is cut by the horizon into visible and invisible halves.
branches.cn: 天空：天球被地平圈分成可见与不可见的两半。

intro.en: Hemisphere joins a Greek prefix for 'half' to the Greek word for 'ball'; the second element also builds the atmosphere and biosphere words.
intro.cn: hemisphere 把希腊「一半」前缀与希腊「球」词连在一起；后一成分还构成 atmosphere 与 biosphere 等词。

latinIntro.en: Greek sphaira 'ball' passed into Latin as sphaera and into English as -sphere; hemi- remains a live prefix in English compounds.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 sphaira「球」传入拉丁作 sphaera，再进入英语作 -sphere；hemi- 在英语复合词中仍是能产前缀。

items.example: The prefix cuts the sphere exactly in two.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把球正好切成两半。

items.example: The root supplies the round shape.
The northern hemisphere is warmer in July.
Hemispheric trade grew after the treaty.
items.exampleCN: 条约签订后半球间贸易增长。

items.example: The child recovered after a hemispherectomy.
items.exampleCN: 这个孩子在半球切除术后康复。

items.example: The biosphere extends through land and sea.
items.exampleCN: 生物圈遍及陆地与海洋。

items.example: Radio signals bounce off the ionosphere.
items.exampleCN: 无线电信号从电离层反射。

definition_zh: 孔；缝隙；（相机）光圈；口径
definition_en: an opening, hole, or gap, especially one that lets light through
core_image: 相机镜头里一开一合的金属叶片
scene: 暗房里红光微亮，摄影师转动镜头上的圆环。 A wide aperture lets in more light.
sceneCN: 这里 aperture 是「光圈」（第 2 个义项：镜头上控制进光量的开孔）；句意为大光圈能放进更多光线。

pos.zh: 孔；缝隙；光圈

derivatives.zh: 同根词，义为「通便的；有开孔作用的」
同根借词，义为「开胃酒」（原义「打开」）

senses.title: An opening or gap
senses.definition: a hole or narrow opening in a surface or structure, especially one admitting air or light
senses.definitionCN: 表面或结构上的孔洞或窄口，尤指可透光透气的
senses.example: Light spilled through a small aperture in the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 光线从墙上的一个小孔中洒进来。
senses.why: From aperire 'to open', the noun names the thing that has been opened.
senses.whyCN: 来自 aperire「打开」，名词指被打开出来的那个口子。

senses.title: The lens opening of a camera
senses.definition: the adjustable opening in a camera lens that controls how much light enters
senses.definitionCN: 相机镜头中可调节的开孔，控制进光量
senses.example: A wide aperture lets in more light.
senses.exampleCN: 大光圈能放进更多光线。
senses.why: The lens contains a literal little opening, so optics borrowed the same word for it.
senses.whyCN: 镜头里确实有一个小开口，光学借用了同一个词来称呼它。

intro.en: Aperture goes back to Latin aperire 'to open', via the Late Latin noun aperture.
intro.cn: aperture 源自拉丁语 aperire「打开」，经后期拉丁语名词 aperture 进入英语。

items.en: The root *per- meant 'to lead or pass over', the base of Latin parire.
items.cn: 词根 *per- 意为「引、过」，是拉丁语 parire 的基础。

items.en: aperire meant 'to open', as in April, the month buds open.
items.cn: aperire 意为「打开」，April（四月）即草木初开之月。

items.en: Late Latin formed apertura, 'an opening', from the verb.
items.cn: 后期拉丁语由该动词构成 apertura「开口」。

items.en: English took the word in late Middle English, first in medicine and architecture.
items.cn: 英语于中古英语晚期借入此词，最早用于医学与建筑。

items.en: Nineteenth-century photography fixed its best-known sense: the lens aperture.
items.cn: 十九世纪的摄影术确立了它最著名的义项：镜头光圈。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the aper- family; the near-meaning group gathers openings of all kinds.
note.cn: 形近组收 aper- 词族；近义组收各种「开口」。

entries.definition: a drink taken before a meal to open the appetite
entries.definitionCN: 开胃酒，同源于 aperire「打开」

entries.definition: an orange-yellow fruit
entries.definitionCN: 杏；只是词形相近，词源亦同出 aperire 一系但意义无关

entries.definition: the boundary line around a shape
entries.definitionCN: 周长；周边，词形相近但词源不同

entries.definition: a gap or hole that allows passage
entries.definitionCN: 开口；空隙，普通用词

entries.definition: an opening of the body or of a tube
entries.definitionCN: （身体或管子的）孔口

entries.definition: an opening that lets air or gas escape
entries.definitionCN: 通风口；排气孔

normalIntro.en: Aperture is the mouth of a camera.
normalIntro.cn: aperture 就是相机的「嘴巴」。

normal.en: Root aper- means open, as in aperitif.
normal.cn: 词根 aper- 表示「打开」，同 aperitif。

normal.en: April opens the year's flowers; aperture opens to light.
normal.cn: April 让百花开放，aperture 向光线开放。

normal.en: Wide aperture = more light; narrow aperture = less.
normal.cn: 大光圈进光多，小光圈进光少。

normal.en: Aperture priority is a standard camera mode.
normal.cn: 光圈优先是相机的标准模式。

normal.en: In building, aperture can be any window-like gap.
normal.cn: 在建筑里 aperture 可指窗状开口。

abstract.en: See metal blades folding open inside a lens.
abstract.cn: 想象镜头内金属叶片张开。

abstract.en: See a keyhole with light leaking through.
abstract.cn: 想象锁孔里漏出的一线光。

abstract.en: See a pupil widening in a dark room.
abstract.cn: 想象暗室中放大的瞳孔。

examples.en: Light spilled through a small aperture in the wall.
examples.cn: 光线从墙上的一个小孔中洒进来。

examples.en: A wide aperture lets in more light.
examples.cn: 大光圈能放进更多光线。

examples.en: She adjusted the aperture before taking the shot.
examples.cn: 她在按下快门前调整了光圈。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿珀彻」——「阿」然「开」一口，「彻」底透进光，正是开孔透光之意。

root: 源自拉丁语 aperire「打开」（印欧词根 *per-「引、过」），经后期拉丁语 apertura「开口」于十五世纪进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: From any physical opening the word narrowed into photography's light-controlling hole.
sensesIntro.cn: 从任何实际的开口，这个词收窄为摄影里控制进光的孔。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hole that decides how much world gets in.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个决定让多少世界进来的孔。

branches.en: a crack in the stone wall
branches.cn: 石墙上的裂缝

branches.en: air through a vent gap
branches.cn: 穿过缝隙的空气

branches.en: blades closing to a pinprick
branches.cn: 叶片收拢成针孔

branches.en: stopping down for depth
branches.cn: 缩小光圈增加景深

branches.en: an opening tuned like an eye
branches.cn: 调得像瞳孔一样的开口

intro.en: A Latin verb turned noun: open, then the opening itself.
intro.cn: 由拉丁动词转来的名词：先「打开」，再指「打开之物」。

latinIntro.en: The aper- root also gives aperitif and aperient.
latinIntro.cn: aper- 词根还派生 aperitif 与 aperient。

definition_zh: 与……一致；与……相符；符合；与……相合；与……相称
definition_en: to agree with or match something such as evidence, a rule, a style or a forecast, so that no contradiction arises
core_image: 两张坐标纸叠在一起，一条曲线来自仪器记录，另一条来自推算，笔尖停在两线完全重合的位置
scene: 实验室的灯一直亮着，值班的人把温度记录纸与模拟输出并排铺在桌上，发现两条曲线的起伏几乎一模一样。 Every reading in the log must be consistent with the simulation before the report is signed.
sceneCN: 这里指观测数据与模拟结果相合（第 1 个义项：与实测证据相符）；句意为在报告签字之前，日志里的每一次读数都必须与模拟结果相符。图中可辨识物件：温度记录纸、模拟曲线、签字笔、封存袋。

pos.zh: 与……一致；符合（系表结构，时态由系动词承担，后接名词、代词或名词性从句）
与……相称（后接风格、身份、惯例等抽象名词）

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「一致性；前后一贯」
去掉系动词后的形容词原形，义为「一致的；相符的」
由形容词加副词尾构成，义为「一贯地；始终如一地」
由否定前缀加形容词构成，义为「不一致的；自相矛盾的」
由否定前缀加名词尾构成，义为「不一致之处」

senses.title: Matching the evidence
senses.definition: to agree with the observed data or the recorded facts
senses.definitionCN: 与观测到的数据或已记录的事实相合
senses.example: Any explanation of the anomaly must be consistent with every measurement taken that night.
senses.exampleCN: 对这一异常的任何解释，都必须与当晚取到的每一次测量相符。
senses.why: The core verb meant to stand together; a claim that stands together with the data is a claim the data will not knock down.
senses.whyCN: 核心动词本义是「站在一起」；一个能与数据站在一起的说法，就是数据推不倒的说法。

senses.title: Following the same rule
senses.definition: to comply with an established rule, code or standard
senses.definitionCN: 遵守既定的规则、规范或标准
senses.example: All new buildings should be consistent with the city's safety code.
senses.exampleCN: 所有新建房屋都应与该市的安全规范相符。
senses.why: Rules are written to hold across many cases, so a single case that fits them can stand beside every other case.
senses.whyCN: 规则要能覆盖许多情形，因此与规则相合的单个情形，可以和其余情形并排站住。

senses.title: Not contradicting itself
senses.definition: to be internally coherent, with no part denying another
senses.definitionCN: 内部自洽，没有任何一部分否定另一部分
senses.example: A sound argument must be consistent with its own premises from the first line to the last.
senses.exampleCN: 一个可靠的论证必须从第一行到最后一行都与自身的前提保持一致。
senses.why: Standing together also means standing together with oneself: the parts of a statement must not pull apart.
senses.whyCN: 「站在一起」也包括与自己站在一起：一个说法的各部分不能各自扯开。

senses.title: Compatible with another theory
senses.definition: to be able to coexist with another account without contradiction
senses.definitionCN: 能与另一种解释共存而不产生矛盾
senses.example: The two models can be consistent with each other only if the second assumption is dropped.
senses.exampleCN: 只有放弃第二个假设，这两个模型才可能与彼此相容。
senses.why: Two accounts are compatible when both can stand on the same ground; where they cannot, one must give way.
senses.whyCN: 两种解释能站在同一块地面上才叫相容；站不住的时候，必须有一方让位。

senses.title: In keeping with a style or character
senses.definition: to match the tone, manner or character of something
senses.definitionCN: 与某物的格调、做法或气质相配
senses.example: The plain wooden benches should be consistent with the meeting house's austere style.
senses.exampleCN: 那些素木长凳应当与聚会所的简朴风格相称。
senses.why: Style is a kind of standing together too: each detail must stand beside the others without looking borrowed.
senses.whyCN: 风格也是一种站在一起：每个细节都要与其余细节并排而不显得是借来的。

senses.title: In line with past practice
senses.definition: to follow the custom or precedent set by earlier decisions
senses.definitionCN: 沿用早先决定所立下的惯例或先例
senses.example: The committee's ruling will be consistent with its decisions over the past decade.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会的裁决将与其过去十年的决定保持一致。
senses.why: Custom is continuity over time: a new decision stands together with the old ones, or the record looks broken.
senses.whyCN: 惯例是时间上的连续：新决定要与旧决定站在一起，否则记录就显得断裂。

senses.title: Within the allowed tolerance
senses.definition: to fall inside the permitted range of variation for a measurement
senses.definitionCN: 测量值处在允许的变动范围之内
senses.example: A shaft that is slightly oval may still be consistent with the tolerance band.
senses.exampleCN: 略微呈椭圆的轴，仍可能落在允许的误差带之内。
senses.why: In manufacture, agreement is numeric: the part stands within a band rather than exactly on a line.
senses.whyCN: 在制造中，一致是数值上的：零件只要站进误差带，而不必正好压线。

senses.title: Matching a legal precedent
senses.definition: to be compatible with a constitution, statute or earlier court ruling
senses.definitionCN: 与宪法、成文法或早先判决相兼容
senses.example: The new statute must be consistent with the constitution as interpreted by earlier courts.
senses.exampleCN: 新法规必须与早先法院所解释的宪法条文相符。
senses.why: Law settles disputes by asking whether a new rule can stand beside the old ones without rewriting them.
senses.whyCN: 法律判断争议的方式，是看新规则能否与旧规则并排站住而不必改写旧规则。

senses.title: Matching what was predicted
senses.definition: to agree with a forecast or a calculated expectation
senses.definitionCN: 与预报或推算出的预期相合
senses.example: The cooling curve should be consistent with the model's prediction if the insulation is intact.
senses.exampleCN: 如果保温层完好，冷却曲线就应与模型的预测相符。
senses.why: A prediction is a claim about a curve not yet drawn; agreement means the drawn curve stands where the claim said it would.
senses.whyCN: 预测是对尚未画出的曲线所作的断言；相符意味着画出的曲线站到了断言所说的位置。

intro.en: The phrase is a grammatical frame around the Latin adjective consistent, which descended from the verb meaning to stand together. The frame itself is an English construction, and its first recorded use in academic prose is dated only approximately.
intro.cn: 这个短语是围绕一个拉丁形容词搭起的语法框架，那个形容词出自表示「一起站立」的动词。框架本身是英语的构造，它在学术文章里最早出现的年代只能给约数。

items.en: Sistere meant to stand, to place or to hold one's ground, and it supplied the standing image behind the whole family.
items.cn: 这个词意为「站立、安放、站住脚」，整个词族的「站」的意象都由它提供。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus sistere produced consistere, to stand together, to hold firm, to remain in one place.
items.cn: 表示「一起」的前缀加「站立」，构成「站在一起、立稳、留在原处」的动词。

items.en: The noun named the state of standing firm, and the participle described something that holds its ground.
items.cn: 相应的名词指「立稳的状态」，分词则形容「站得住的东西」。

items.en: English took the adjective by way of French in the sixteenth century, first for things that hold together, then for statements that do not contradict each other.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪经法语引入这个形容词，先指「结实地连在一起的东西」，后指「不自相矛盾的说法」。

items.en: The frame be plus the adjective plus with became the standard way to say that a finding, a rule or a style agrees with something else. The exact first citation of the frame is uncertain.
items.cn: 由系动词、形容词与介词构成的这个框架，成为表示「结论、规则或风格与某物相合」的标准说法。该框架最早的书证年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the same Latin standing root but splits into two unlike meanings; the second group holds ordinary ways of saying that two things agree.
note.cn: 第一组共享同一个拉丁「站立」词根，却分成两个完全不同的意思；第二组是表示「两物相合」的普通说法。

entries.definition: Built on the same verb, it means to be made up of parts, not to agree with something. A report can consist of five chapters and still not be consistent with the evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 由同一个动词构成，意思却是「由部分组成」，并非「与某物一致」。一份报告可以由五章构成，却仍与证据不符。

entries.definition: The bare adjective describes a thing or a set of results that holds together; the phrase adds the second party that it agrees with.
entries.definitionCN: 单独的形容词形容某物或某组结果自身站得住；短语则补出它所相合的那一方。

entries.definition: The noun names the quality of agreement, as in the consistency of the results; it cannot take the whole phrase's object directly.
entries.definitionCN: 名词指「一致」这一性质，如结果的一致性；它不能像短语那样直接带出所相合的对象。

entries.definition: The negative adjective says that two things cannot stand together, which is exactly what the phrase denies.
entries.definitionCN: 否定形容词表示两物无法并立，正是这个短语所肯定的反面。

entries.definition: A formal verb phrase for agreeing with facts or principles; it is close in meaning but far less common in quantitative writing.
entries.definitionCN: 正式地表示与事实或原则相合，意思接近，但在定量写作中远不如本短语常用。

entries.definition: Literally to bring into one line; used for plans and interests that point the same way, with less stress on factual proof.
entries.definitionCN: 字面是「排成一条线」，多用于方向、利益一致，对事实证据的强调较弱。

entries.definition: To follow a rule or pattern exactly; it stresses obedience to a standard rather than agreement among findings.
entries.definitionCN: 指严格遵照规则或范式，强调对标准的服从，而不是结论之间的一致。

entries.definition: The everyday verb for two things fitting each other; it is neutral in tone and lacks the phrase's academic register.
entries.definitionCN: 日常表示两物相配的动词，语气中性，没有这个短语的学术语域。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the two overlapping curves, the code book, the committee record and the tolerance band.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用两条重合的曲线、规范手册、委员会记录与误差带四个场景。

normal.en: Two curves laid on one sheet: where they overlap, the reading agrees with the model.
normal.cn: 两张曲线铺在同一张纸上：重叠之处，读数就与模型相符。

normal.en: A new building checked against the code book, clause by clause.
normal.cn: 新楼对着规范手册，一条一条核对。

normal.en: A statement read twice: the second half must not deny the first.
normal.cn: 一句话读两遍：后半句不能否定前半句。

normal.en: A committee ruling placed beside ten years of earlier rulings.
normal.cn: 把委员会的新裁决，摆到过去十年的旧裁决旁边。

normal.en: A shaft measured against the tolerance band, not against a perfect line.
normal.cn: 量轴时对着误差带，而不是对着一条完美的线。

abstract.en: Agreement is not sameness: two things can differ in shape and still stand together.
abstract.cn: 一致不是相同：两样东西形状不同，仍可以站在一起。

abstract.en: Every field draws a line and then asks which results may stand on it.
abstract.cn: 每个领域都先画一条线，再问哪些结果可以站到线上。

abstract.en: A claim that agrees with everything agrees with nothing in particular.
abstract.cn: 与一切都相符的说法，其实不与任何具体事物相符。

examples.en: The isotope ratio must be consistent with the age assigned to the layer.
examples.cn: 同位素比值必须与该层位所定的年代相符。

examples.en: Her account of the meeting should be consistent with the minutes kept by the secretary.
examples.cn: 她对那次会议的叙述，应与秘书所作的记录一致。

examples.en: A policy can be consistent with the law and still be unpopular.
examples.cn: 一项政策可以合乎法律，却依然不得人心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「比 肯西斯滕特 威兹」：把「站在一起」记成两条线站到同一条线上——站得齐，才叫一致

root: 核心动词出自拉丁语「一起站立」，由表示「共同」的前缀加表示「站立」的词根构成，本义是「立稳、站得住」，引申为「前后相合」。该短语是英语学术写作的固定框架，由系动词、形容词与介词三层组成，时态由系动词承担。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses move from proof to propriety: agreement with data, with a rule, with itself, with another theory, with a style, with past practice, with a tolerance band, with precedent, and with a forecast.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从证据走到得体：与数据相符、与规则相符、与自身自洽、与另一理论相容、与风格相称、与旧例一致、落在误差带内、合于判例、与预测相符。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two curves drawn on one sheet, one from an instrument and one from a calculation, meeting along the same line.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条曲线画在同一张纸上，一条来自仪器，一条来自推算，沿着同一条线重合。

branches.en: THE DRAWN LINE: a reading or a forecast must land where the claim said it would.
branches.cn: 画出的线：读数或预测必须落在断言所说的位置。

branches.en: THE STANDING RULE: a case fits the written code, or fits the unwritten custom of earlier cases.
branches.cn: 站得住的规则：或合于成文规范，或合于旧例的不成文惯例。

branches.en: THE SELF AND THE OTHER: a statement must not deny its own parts, and two accounts must not deny each other.
branches.cn: 自身与对方：一个说法不能否定自己的各部分，两种解释也不能互相否定。

branches.en: THE SETTING: style and character are agreement of tone rather than of fact.
branches.cn: 场合：风格与身份的一致，是语气上的一致，而非事实上的相符。

branches.en: THE BAND AND THE BENCH: a part sits inside a tolerance band, a statute sits beside earlier rulings.
branches.cn: 误差带与判席：零件站进误差带，法规站到旧判决旁边。

intro.en: This phrase is a Latin standing word inside an English frame; its family covers the verb, the adjective, the noun and their negatives.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁语的「站立」之词装进英语框架；词族覆盖动词、形容词、名词及各自的否定形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin consistere and its noun consistentia supplied the adjective, and English added its own endings around them.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「一起站立」动词及其名词提供了形容词的底子，英语又在其外围加上自己的词尾。

items.example: It binds the parts into one standing whole.

items.meaning: to stand, to hold one's ground
items.example: The standing image at the centre of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这是整个词族中心的「站立」意象。

items.example: The source of the English verb and adjective.
items.exampleCN: 英语动词与形容词的共同来源。

items.example: The stem that English took as an adjective.

items.example: It turns the stem into a describing word.

items.example: It names the state of standing firm.

senses.title: Blind with light
senses.definition: to make someone unable to see because of bright light

senses.example: The headlights dazzled the cyclist.
senses.exampleCN: 车灯晃得骑车人睁不开眼。
senses.why: A white starburst in the eyes.

senses.title: Amaze with skill

intro.en: Dazzle is daze plus the repeated-action ending -le.
intro.cn: dazzle 由 daze 加表示反复动作的词尾 -le 构成。

items.en: Dasi named a stunned person.
items.cn: dasi 指发懵的人。

items.en: Dasen meant to stun with a blow.
items.cn: dasen 意为一击使人发懵。

items.en: Dasel added the repeated ending -el.
items.cn: 十五世纪 dasel 加上反复词尾 -el。

items.en: Dazzle came to mean blinding with light.
items.cn: 十六世纪 dazzle 转为「以强光晃眼」。

items.en: Dazzle gained the sense of amazing skill.

definition_zh: 减法；减法运算过程；扣除额；减少
definition_en: the arithmetic operation of taking one quantity away from another, or the amount so taken
core_image: 黑板上的一列数字被划掉一行，剩下的那一行写在横线下面
scene: 数学课上，老师让学生用竖式完成一道三位数的减法。 The class practised subtraction with three-digit numbers.
sceneCN: 这里指「减法这项运算本身」（第 1 个义项：减法运算）；句意为全班练习三位数的减法。可辨识物件：黑板、粉笔、竖式、横线。

pos.zh: 减法；扣除；减少；被减去的量

collocations.phrase: subtraction of one number from another
collocations.zh: 用一个数减去另一个数

senses.title: The arithmetic operation
senses.definition: the operation of taking one number away from another
senses.definitionCN: 从一个数里拿走另一个数的运算
senses.example: Subtraction is taught alongside addition in the first year.
senses.exampleCN: 减法在一年级就与加法一起教。
senses.why: The noun names the operation itself, built directly on the Latin verb for drawing away.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词直接由拉丁动词「抽走」构成，指运算本身。

senses.title: The working of such a problem
senses.definition: the written or mental working by which such a problem is solved
senses.definitionCN: 解这类题时写出来或心算的过程
senses.example: Her subtraction was neat, with every borrow marked.
senses.exampleCN: 她的减法写得整齐，每次借位都标了出来。
senses.why: English lets the name of the operation also cover the steps taken to carry it out.
senses.whyCN: 英语让运算的名称同时覆盖执行它的步骤。

senses.title: The amount taken away
senses.definition: the quantity that is removed from a larger one
senses.definitionCN: 从较大量中取走的那份量
senses.example: The subtraction from the budget was larger than expected.
senses.exampleCN: 预算被削减的数额比预期更大。
senses.why: The same noun serves for the act and for its result, a pattern English uses constantly.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词既指动作也指结果，这是英语常见的做法。

senses.title: A reduction in amount
senses.definition: a decrease in an amount, especially one made deliberately
senses.definitionCN: 数量的减少，尤指有意造成的减少
senses.example: A subtraction of ten staff changed the office entirely.
senses.exampleCN: 减掉十名员工让办公室完全变了样。
senses.why: Counting the removed part turns naturally into naming the reduction itself.
senses.whyCN: 为被拿走的部分计数，自然就转为命名这次减少。

senses.title: The minus sign in notation
senses.definition: the sign used to mark this operation in written arithmetic
senses.definitionCN: 书面算术中标记这一运算的符号
senses.example: A subtraction sign is a short horizontal stroke.
senses.exampleCN: 减号是一道短短的横线。
senses.why: The sign is called by the name of the operation it performs, a common shorthand in mathematics.
senses.whyCN: 这个符号以它所执行的运算命名，是数学里常见的简写。

senses.title: A deduction in accounts
senses.definition: an item deducted before a balance is struck
senses.definitionCN: 结账之前被扣除的项目
senses.example: The statement lists each subtraction from the gross sum.
senses.exampleCN: 账单把从总额中扣掉的每一项都列了出来。
senses.why: Bookkeeping treats every removal as a named entry, so the operation becomes a line in a ledger.
senses.whyCN: 记账把每次移除都当成一个有名字的条目，于是运算变成账簿上的一行。

senses.title: Finding what remains by exclusion
senses.definition: the method of finding what is left by ruling out what it is not
senses.definitionCN: 通过排除「不是什么」来求出剩下的是什么
senses.example: The detective worked by subtraction, discarding every impossible route.
senses.exampleCN: 侦探用排除法，把每条不可能的路都划掉。
senses.why: The metaphor extends the arithmetic: whatever is ruled out is taken away until one answer remains.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把算术延伸开：凡被排除的都被拿走，直到只剩一个答案。

senses.title: Stripping away the unnecessary
senses.definition: the act of removing whatever is not essential
senses.definitionCN: 去掉一切非必要成分的行为
senses.example: The final edit was pure subtraction, cutting every line that repeated the point.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一轮修改纯粹是做减法，删掉了每一句重复的话。
senses.why: With numbers gone, subtraction becomes the discipline of taking away rather than the count of what is left.
senses.whyCN: 数字消失之后，减法变成「取走」的自律，而不是对剩余之物的计数。

intro.en: Subtraction comes from Late Latin subtractio, a noun of action from subtrahere 'to draw away'. The verb is sub- 'from below' plus trahere 'to draw'; the earlier origin of trahere is unsettled.
intro.cn: subtraction 出自晚期拉丁名词 subtractio，是 subtrahere「抽走」的动作名词；该动词由 sub-「从下面」加 trahere「拉」构成，trahere 的更早来源无定论。

items.en: Trahere meant 'to draw, pull'. Its pre-Latin origin is not established, so any older form cited for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: trahere 意为「拉、拖」。它在拉丁语之前的来源未获证明，凡为其引出的更古老形式都属重构形式。

items.en: Sub- 'from below' plus trahere gave subtrahere 'to draw away, take away'.
items.cn: sub-「从下面」加 trahere 得出 subtrahere「抽走、拿走」。

items.en: The action noun subtractio named the drawing away itself; English took the noun rather than the Latin verb form.
items.cn: 动作名词 subtractio 指「抽走」这件事本身；英语取的是这个名词，而非拉丁动词原形。

items.en: The noun appeared in English in the fifteenth century, at first in general use and only later as a school term.
items.cn: 这个名词在十五世纪进入英语，起初是一般用法，后来才成为课堂术语。

items.en: Printing and schooling fixed subtraction as the standard name of the operation from the seventeenth century onward.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，印刷与学校教育使 subtraction 固定为这项运算的标准名称。

items.en: The figurative sense of ruling things out till one answer remains is modern and rests on the arithmetic image.
items.cn: 「不断排除直到只剩一个答案」的比喻用法属现代发展，依托于算术形象。

note.en: Group one holds words that wear the same noun ending or come from the same verb; group two holds words for a decrease or a deduction.
note.cn: 第一组是共用同一名词词尾、或出自同一动词的词；第二组是表示「减少」或「扣除」的近义词。

entries.definition: The inverse operation, built on a different Latin verb; the matching ending hides a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 与之相反的运算，出自另一个拉丁动词；相同的词尾掩盖了不同的词根。

entries.definition: The verb from which the noun is formed; the noun names the operation, the verb the act.
entries.definitionCN: 名词由这个动词构成；名词指运算，动词指动作。

entries.definition: The technical name for the quantity taken away, from the same Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 被取走那个量的专门名称，出自同一个拉丁动词。

entries.definition: From de- plus ducere 'lead': a leading away, hence an amount deducted; the ending matches but the root does not.
entries.definitionCN: 由 de- 加 ducere「引导」构成，意为「引走」，引申为扣除额；词尾相同而词根不同。

entries.definition: A general word for making an amount smaller, whether by taking away or by lowering a rate.
entries.definitionCN: 使数量变小的通称，无论靠拿走一部分还是靠降低比率。

entries.definition: To become or make less, used of sizes, rates and numbers without any arithmetic frame.
entries.definitionCN: 变小或使变小，用于尺寸、比率与数量，不带算术框架。

entries.definition: The act of moving something out of its place, usually physical.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物移出原位的动作，通常指实物。

entries.definition: An informal word for a reduction ordered by someone, as in a cut in funding.
entries.definitionCN: 由某方决定削减的口语说法，如削减经费。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定说法与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The noun is the verb plus an action ending, so it names the operation rather than the person doing it.
normal.cn: 名词由动词加动作词尾构成，因此它指运算，而不是做运算的人。

normal.en: The family runs subtract, subtraction, subtractive, subtrahend and subtractional.
normal.cn: 同族词串成一条线：减去、减法、减去的、减数、减法上的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the classroom: a subtraction problem, a subtraction sign, repeated subtraction.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出课堂场景：减法题、减号、连减。

normal.en: Every word built on the same root differs by prefix: away, together, out, apart, from below.
normal.cn: 同根词只靠前缀区别：离开、一起、向外、分开、从下面。

normal.en: In a written sum the removed number is the subtrahend, a Latin tag meaning 'to be subtracted'.
normal.cn: 在竖式里被拿走的那个数是「减数」，这个拉丁标签意为「待减去者」。
