circus 产生 circus 与 circle。
proximus 产生 proximity 与 approximate。

definition_zh: 广告主；登广告的人；投放广告的企业
definition_en: the person or firm that pays for and places a public notice promoting something
core_image: 一间办公室里的人把支票和一张海报一起递出去，买下别人的目光
scene: 会议室里，市场部把钱和一张海报一起推到桌上，买下整条街的目光。 The advertiser asked for a full page opposite the crossword.
sceneCN: 会议室里，市场部把钱和一张海报一起推上桌，买下整条街的目光；句中的这个词指「出钱投放广告的一方」（第 1 个义项：付费让告示出现在媒体上的人或企业）。图中可辨识物件：会议桌、支票、海报、版面样张、字幕格。

pos.zh: 广告主；出钱登广告的人或企业（可数）
登分类广告的人（卖房、招人、寻物）

forms.label: 形容词（由广告主出资的）

senses.title: The party that pays for the notice
senses.definition: a person or firm that pays to have a promotional notice placed in a medium
senses.definitionCN: 出钱让推销告示出现在媒体上的人或企业
senses.example: The advertiser asked for a full page opposite the crossword.
senses.exampleCN: 广告主要求在填字游戏对面买一整版。
senses.why: The -er suffix marks the doer; here the deed is paying for attention, so the doer is the buyer of space.
senses.whyCN: -er 后缀标示动作的发出者；这里的动作是「花钱买注意力」，所以发出者就是买版面的人。

senses.title: The media buyer acting for a firm
senses.titleCN: 替公司买版面的媒介执行者
senses.definition: the marketing staff member who negotiates and buys space or time on behalf of a company
senses.definitionCN: 代表公司谈判并购买版面或时段的营销人员
senses.example: As the advertiser's agent, she books all the radio slots.
senses.exampleCN: 作为广告主的代理，她预订了所有电台时段。
senses.why: The payer can act through an agent, and the agent still speaks with the payer's name on the contract.
senses.whyCN: 出钱方可以委托代理人行事，而合同上写的仍是出钱方的名字。

senses.title: One who places a classified line
senses.definition: a private person who pays for a short notice to sell, let or find something
senses.definitionCN: 花钱登一条短告示，用来出售、出租或寻找某物的私人
senses.example: The advertiser withdrew the notice after the bike was sold.
senses.exampleCN: 自行车卖掉后，登广告的人撤下了那则告示。
senses.why: A single line in the classified column makes an ordinary person an advertiser for a week.
senses.whyCN: 分类版上的一行字，就能让一个普通人在一周内成为广告主。

senses.title: The party recruiting
senses.definition: an employer or organization that advertises a vacancy or a call for volunteers
senses.definitionCN: 登广告发布空缺职位或招募志愿者的雇主或机构
senses.example: The advertiser offered a salary well above the local average.
senses.exampleCN: 招募方开出的薪水远高于当地平均。
senses.why: A vacancy notice is still a paid notice, so the employer takes the same name as a soap seller.
senses.whyCN: 招聘告示仍是付费告示，所以雇主与卖肥皂的人共用同一个称呼。

senses.title: Anyone who advertises, informally
senses.definition: in loose speech, any person or group that promotes something in public
senses.definitionCN: 口语中宽泛地指任何公开宣传某事的人或团体
senses.example: Every advertiser in town wanted a place on that wall.
senses.exampleCN: 镇上每个做广告的人都想在那面墙上占一个位置。
senses.why: Loose speech drops the payment condition and keeps only the act of promoting.
senses.whyCN: 口语丢掉了「付费」这个条件，只保留了「宣传」这个动作。

senses.title: The medium's client
senses.definition: seen from the media side, the customer who buys its space or time
senses.definitionCN: 从媒体一侧看，购买其版面或时段的客户
senses.example: The station lost its biggest advertiser in the spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这家电台在春天失去了最大的广告客户。
senses.why: The relation has two ends: the firm is the seller of goods, but the client of the newspaper.
senses.whyCN: 这层关系有两端：这家公司在卖货，却是报纸的客户。

senses.title: A promoter of an idea
senses.definition: a group that pays to spread a cause or a public message rather than a product
senses.definitionCN: 付费传播某项事业或公共信息、而非商品的团体
senses.example: The health charity became the largest advertiser on the bus network.
senses.exampleCN: 那家健康慈善机构成了公交网络上最大的广告主。
senses.why: If a cause can buy attention, the buyer of that attention is an advertiser just the same.
senses.whyCN: 如果一项事业也能买注意力，那么买这份注意力的人同样就是广告主。

senses.title: The sponsor behind a message
senses.definition: the backer whose money carries a message, credited at the end of it
senses.definitionCN: 出钱承载某条信息、并在信息末尾被署名的一方
senses.example: The advertiser's name appears in the last frame of the film.
senses.exampleCN: 广告主的名字出现在影片最后一帧。
senses.why: Sponsorship is payment for attention with the name made visible, which is the advertiser's defining wish.
senses.whyCN: 赞助就是花钱买注意力并把名字露出来，这正是广告主最根本的诉求。

intro.en: Advertiser is a plain English derivative: the verb plus the agent suffix. Its meaning narrowed as the verb narrowed.
intro.cn: advertiser 是一个朴素的英语派生词：动词加施事后缀。它的词义随着动词一起收窄。

items.en: Latin vertere 'to turn' is the distant root, also behind versus and divert.
items.cn: 拉丁 vertere「转」是更远的词根，也藏在 versus 与 divert 背后。

items.en: Ad- 'toward' plus vertere gave advertere 'to turn toward'. The idea reached English through the French verb avertir.
items.cn: ad-「朝向」加 vertere 构成 advertere「转向」。这个意念经法语动词 avertir 传到英语。

items.en: The suffix -er forms nouns for the doer of a verb, as in teacher and buyer. Attached to advertise it yields advertiser.
items.cn: 后缀 -er 为动词的施事造名词，如 teacher 与 buyer。加到 advertise 上就得到 advertiser。

items.en: The earliest recorded use names a person who gives notice, matching the then-current meaning of the verb.
items.cn: 最早有记录的用法指「发出通知的人」，与当时动词的意思一致。

items.en: When advertise came to mean publishing a notice of goods, advertiser came to mean the party paying for that notice.
items.cn: 当 advertise 变成「刊登商品告示」，advertiser 也随之变成「为那则告示付钱的一方」。

items.en: In the modern trade the word usually means the client of a medium or agency, and it appears in compounds such as advertiser-funded.
items.cn: 在现代行业里，这个词通常指媒体或代理公司的客户，并出现在 advertiser-funded 这类复合词中。

note.en: Group one is built from the same verb; group two names neighbouring roles in the same trade.
note.cn: 第一组由同一个动词构成；第二组是同一行业里相邻的角色。

entries.definition: The activity or industry; it has no doer and cannot be counted as a person.
entries.definitionCN: 指活动或行业；它没有施事者，也不能当作一个人来数。

entries.definition: The notice itself, not the party that pays for it.
entries.definitionCN: 指告示本身，而不是为它付钱的一方。

entries.definition: The action; the -er noun adds a person who performs it.
entries.definitionCN: 动作；加 -er 后指执行这个动作的人。

entries.definition: One who gives advice, from Latin videre 'to see'; the spelling differs by a single letter and the meaning is far apart.
entries.definitionCN: 给建议的人，出自拉丁 videre「看」；拼写只差一个字母，意思相去甚远。

entries.definition: A backer who pays to be linked with an event or programme, often without a standalone notice.
entries.definitionCN: 出钱与某活动或节目建立关联的赞助者，往往没有独立的告示。

entries.definition: The advertiser as seen by the agency that serves it, one step further from the medium.
entries.definitionCN: 从为其服务的代理公司角度看，广告主就是客户，比媒体的视角又远一层。

entries.definition: The person who plans the whole selling effort, of which placing notices is one task.
entries.definitionCN: 筹划整个销售努力的人，投放告示只是其中一项任务。

entries.definition: The owner of the medium that sells the space; the advertiser is its customer, not its peer.
entries.definitionCN: 出售版面的媒体所有者；广告主是它的客户，而不是同类。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real suffix function, real compounds and real roles in the trade.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的后缀功能、真实的复合词与行业中的真实角色。

normal.en: advertise + -er: the -er marks the one who pays for the notice.
normal.cn: advertise 加 -er：-er 标示出为告示付钱的那一方。

normal.en: The family ladder is advertise → advertiser → advertisement → advertising.
normal.cn: 这一族的梯子是 advertise → advertiser → advertisement → advertising。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the role: a major advertiser, the advertiser's budget, attract advertisers.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示角色：大广告主、广告主的预算、吸引广告主。

normal.en: Advertiser-funded marks the model where the payer, not the reader, covers the cost.
normal.cn: advertiser-funded 标示那种由出钱方而非读者承担成本的模式。

normal.en: Do not mix it with adviser: one pays for space, the other gives advice.
normal.cn: 别把它和 adviser 混起来：一个买版面，一个给建议。

abstract.en: Picture a hand writing a cheque and, in the same motion, pointing at a poster.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在写支票，同一个动作里又指向一张海报。

abstract.en: The advertiser never appears in the message as a person, only as the name at the edge of it.
abstract.cn: 广告主从不在信息里作为一个人出现，只在信息的边缘留下名字。

abstract.en: So the word marks the edge where money meets attention.
abstract.cn: 所以这个词标出的正是金钱与注意力相接的那条边。

examples.en: The magazine's advertisers demanded a cheaper rate for the winter issues.
examples.cn: 这家杂志的广告主要求冬季几期降价。

examples.en: As the biggest advertiser in the region, the brewery could choose its slots.
examples.cn: 作为本区最大的广告主，那家啤酒厂可以挑时段。

examples.en: Each advertiser receives a monthly report on how many people saw the notice.
examples.cn: 每位广告主每月都会收到一份报告，说明有多少人看到了那则告示。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德-歪台泽」——阿德歪着身子把台子上的钱推出去，买下别人的目光 → advertiser 广告主

root: advertise + -er（施事后缀）；advertise 出自拉丁 advertere「转向、把注意力引向」= ad- + vertere「转」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses keep one role: the party whose money turns attention. The role shifts only in who fills it — a firm, an agent, a private seller, an employer, a cause or a sponsor.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项守住同一个角色：出钱把注意力转过来的那一方。变的只是谁来担任——企业、代理人、私人卖家、雇主、某项事业或赞助商。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: money leaves one hand and attention arrives from many eyes.
core.cn: 核心意象：钱从一只手出去，注意力从许多双眼睛回来。

branches.en: TWO SIDES OF ONE CONTRACT: the buyer of space is the customer of the medium.
branches.cn: 同一份合同的两面：买版面的人就是媒体的客户。

branches.en: DELEGATED PURSE: an agent spends the firm's money and signs in the firm's name.
branches.cn: 受托的钱包：代理人花公司的钱，用公司的名义签字。

branches.en: SMALL AND LARGE PAYERS: one line in the classifieds or a salary advertisement both buy a slot.
branches.cn: 小额与大额付钱者：分类栏里的一行字和一则薪资广告，买的都是同一个位置。

branches.en: LOOSE SPEECH: drop the payment and only the promoting remains.
branches.cn: 口语宽用：去掉付费，只剩下宣传。

branches.en: CAUSE AND NAME: a charity buys attention for an idea, and a sponsor buys the visibility of its own name.
branches.cn: 事业与名字：慈善机构为理念买注意力，赞助商为自己的名字买曝光。

intro.en: Advertiser adds a common English agent suffix to a Latin-derived verb, so the word reads as 'the one who advertises'.
intro.cn: advertiser 给一个拉丁来源的动词加上常见英语施事后缀，于是整个词读作「做广告的那个人」。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is advertere 'to turn toward' (ad- plus vertere); the suffix -er is native English word-building.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基是 advertere「转向」（ad- 加 vertere）；后缀 -er 则是英语本土的构词手段。

items.meaning: the person or firm that does something
items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a role.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成一个角色。

items.example: Convert and divert carry it too.
items.exampleCN: convert 与 divert 也带着它。
他们做广告以触达买家。
广告主通过了这版画面。
广告为这项服务提供资金。

items.example: The advertisement ran on page five.

items.exampleCN: 那则广告带来十个电话。
发布之后出现了负面评论。

definition_zh: 有机物、有机质；来源于生物的残体及其腐解产物
definition_en: material derived from living things, fresh or decayed, present in soil, water or sediment
core_image: 苗床边撒下一把深褐色碎屑，翻进土里后蚯蚓立刻围过来
scene: 农技员在苗床边抓起一把深褐色的碎屑撒进土里，翻土后蚯蚓很快围了过来，说 A handful of organic matter feeds the worms before it feeds the crop.
sceneCN: 这里 organic matter 指「来源于生物的残体及其腐解产物」，取第 1 个义项（土壤有机质整体）；句意为一把有机质先养活蚯蚓，然后才养活作物。图中可辨识物件：碎屑、苗床、翻土、蚯蚓。

pos.zh: 有机物、有机质（不可数，土壤学、生态学与水质用语）

senses.title: Living and dead biological material in soil
senses.definition: all material in soil that came from organisms, from living roots to fully decayed residue
senses.definitionCN: 土壤中全部来自生物的物质，从活根一直到完全腐解的残余
senses.example: Soil organic matter is the main reserve of nitrogen in most fields.
senses.exampleCN: 土壤有机质是大多数田地里氮的主要储备。
senses.why: Organic marks a biological origin, matter marks the physical stuff, so the phrase covers the whole range at once.
senses.whyCN: organic 标明生物来源，matter 标明物质实体，因此这个短语一次覆盖整个范围。

senses.title: The living fraction
senses.titleCN: 活性部分：活根与土壤生物
senses.definition: roots, fungi, bacteria and soil animals that are part of the organic pool while alive
senses.definitionCN: 活着时即属于有机库的根、真菌、细菌与土壤动物
senses.example: Living organic matter releases sugars into the soil within hours.
senses.exampleCN: 活体有机质在几小时内就把糖释放进土里。
senses.why: The pool is defined by origin rather than by life state, so an organism counts before it dies.
senses.whyCN: 这个库以来源定义而不以生死定义，因此生物在死前就已计入。

senses.title: The stable humified fraction
senses.definition: the dark, slow-turning portion that remains after most material has decomposed
senses.definitionCN: 大部分物质腐解后留下、颜色深且周转缓慢的部分
senses.example: Most of the organic matter in the old pasture was stable humus.
senses.exampleCN: 这片老牧场的大部分有机质是稳定的腐殖质。
senses.why: Each year's input loses its easy parts and leaves a resistant core, so the pool splits into fast and slow fractions.
senses.whyCN: 每年的输入先失去易分解部分，留下抗分解的核心，因此这个库分成了快与慢两部分。

senses.title: Dissolved organic matter
senses.definition: organic compounds small enough to pass a fine filter, carried in soil water or streams
senses.definitionCN: 小到能通过细滤膜的有机化合物，随土壤水或溪流迁移
senses.example: Dissolved organic matter gave the stream its brown colour.
senses.exampleCN: 溶解态有机质让这条溪流呈褐色。
senses.why: Water carries the soluble part away, so analysts filter samples and treat what passes as a separate pool.
senses.whyCN: 水把可溶部分带走，因此分析者过滤样品，并把透过的部分当作另一个库。

senses.title: Particulate organic matter
senses.definition: recognisable fragments of plant or animal material held between soil grains
senses.definitionCN: 夹在土粒之间、仍可辨认的动植物残片
senses.example: Particulate organic matter was easy to see in the sandy soil.
senses.exampleCN: 在砂质土里，颗粒态有机质很容易看见。
senses.why: Coarse fragments remain distinct from the fine matrix, so a size cut separates this pool from the dissolved one.
senses.whyCN: 粗碎片与细基质界限分明，因此按粒径切分就把这个库与溶解态分开。

senses.title: A fertility indicator
senses.titleCN: 有机质含量与肥力指标
senses.definition: the measured percentage used to judge nutrient supply, structure and water holding
senses.definitionCN: 用来判断养分供给、结构与保水能力的实测百分比
senses.example: Organic matter content had dropped below one per cent after years of burning.
senses.exampleCN: 连年焚烧之后，有机质含量降到百分之一以下。
senses.why: A single figure summarises several benefits, which is why soil tests report it before anything else.
senses.whyCN: 一个数字就概括了好几项好处，因此土壤检测总把它列在最前面。

senses.title: Organic matter in water
senses.definition: the organic load in water or waste water, measured by how much oxygen its decay demands
senses.definitionCN: 水或废水中的有机负荷，以其腐解所需氧气量来衡量
senses.example: Organic matter in the discharge raised the oxygen demand sharply.
senses.exampleCN: 排放水中的有机物让需氧量急剧上升。
senses.why: Microbes consume oxygen while breaking the material down, so its amount can be read as an oxygen figure.
senses.whyCN: 微生物分解这些物质时要耗氧，因此其含量可以换算成一个需氧数值。

senses.title: Buried organic matter in sediments
senses.titleCN: 沉积物与烃源岩中的有机质
senses.definition: organic material buried in muds and rocks, which over geological time becomes oil or gas
senses.definitionCN: 埋在泥与岩石中的有机物质，经地质时间可变成石油或天然气
senses.example: The shale is rich in organic matter that never fully decayed.
senses.exampleCN: 这层页岩富含未曾完全腐解的有机质。
senses.why: Burial cuts off oxygen, so decay stops part way and the residue is cooked into hydrocarbons.
senses.whyCN: 埋藏隔绝了氧，腐解半途停止，残余物以后被热解成烃类。

intro.en: Organic comes from Greek organon, an instrument or organ, with Latin -icus; matter comes from Latin materia, timber or substance, from mater, mother. The phrase is a modern scientific pairing.
intro.cn: organic 出自希腊 organon「工具、器官」，加拉丁 -icus；matter 出自拉丁 materia「木料、物质」，源于 mater「母亲」。这个短语是近代科学的搭配。

items.en: Organon meant a tool or instrument, and later an organ of the body, since an organ is the body's instrument.
items.cn: organon 意为工具、器具，后来指身体器官，因为器官正是身体的工具。

items.en: Latin organicus rendered the Greek adjective, and English organic first meant relating to bodily organs before it meant relating to living things in general.
items.cn: 拉丁 organicus 转写了这个希腊形容词，英语 organic 最初指与身体器官有关，后来才泛指与生物有关。

items.en: Materia meant timber, building material and substance, from mater, mother, since material is what things are made from.
items.cn: materia 意为木料、建筑材料与物质，出自 mater「母亲」，因为材料正是造物所出之处。

items.en: Nineteenth-century chemistry needed a term for biological residue in soil and water, and organic matter supplied it without naming any single compound.
items.cn: 十九世纪的化学需要为土壤与水中的生物残余找一个说法，organic matter 正好提供了这个既不指名某化合物的词。

items.en: Twentieth-century research split the phrase into dissolved and particulate pools and added the buried organic matter of petroleum geology.
items.cn: 二十世纪的研究把这个短语分为溶解态与颗粒态，并增加了石油地质学中的埋藏有机质。

note.en: Group one holds the pairs and opposites that sit closest to this phrase; group two holds specific organic materials that are often used loosely in its place.
note.cn: 第一组是与该短语最贴近的配对与对立说法；第二组是常被随手代替它的具体有机材料。

entries.definition: Material not derived from organisms, such as minerals and salts; the pair defines the boundary of the concept.
entries.definitionCN: 非来源于生物的物质，如矿物与盐；这一对说法界定概念边界。

entries.definition: Relating to living things or carbon compounds; it can describe farming or food without naming any material.
entries.definitionCN: 与生物或碳化合物有关的；可不指名任何材料而形容农业或食品。

entries.definition: An individual living thing; organic matter may come from organisms but is not itself one.
entries.definitionCN: 单个生物体；有机质可以来自生物体，但它本身不是生物体。

entries.definition: Any substance used or present; on its own it carries no biological meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 任何被使用或存在的物质；单独使用时不含生物含义。

entries.definition: The stable dark end product of decomposition; it is part of organic matter, not the whole of it.
entries.definitionCN: 腐解稳定的深色末端产物；它是有机质的一部分，而非全部。

entries.definition: The mass of living organisms or of material recently derived from them, usually measured as fuel or energy.
entries.definitionCN: 活生物体或新近由生物来源的物质的量，通常作为燃料或能量计量。

entries.definition: Organic waste rotted under controlled conditions; it is added to soil as a source of organic matter.
entries.definitionCN: 在受控条件下腐解的有机废弃物；作为有机质来源加入土壤。

entries.definition: Dead plant material lying on the surface before decay; it is the input that becomes organic matter.
entries.definitionCN: 腐解前落在地表的枯死植物材料；它是变成有机质的输入。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek organ word, the real Latin material word and the real soil-testing pairs.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊「器官」词、真实的拉丁「材料」词，以及真实的土壤检测用语。

normal.en: Organic means from an organism, matter means the stuff, so the phrase is literally living-origin stuff.
normal.cn: organic 意为来自生物，matter 意为物质，因此这个短语字面就是「生物来源的东西」。

normal.en: Organic matter and inorganic matter are the two halves of any soil test.
normal.cn: 有机质与无机质是任何土壤检测的两半。

normal.en: Three pools in one phrase: living, particulate and dissolved.
normal.cn: 一个短语里有三个库：活的、颗粒的、溶解的。

normal.en: Humus is the stable fraction, not a synonym for the whole phrase.
normal.cn: 腐殖质是稳定部分，而不是整个短语的同义词。

normal.en: Buried organic matter is the beginning of oil and gas.
normal.cn: 被埋藏的有机质是石油与天然气的起点。

abstract.en: Picture a handful of crumbs that worms recognise before plants do.
abstract.cn: 想象一把碎屑，蚯蚓比植物更早认出它。

abstract.en: Picture a dark stain in a stream that came from a forest floor miles away.
abstract.cn: 想象溪水里的一道褐色，来自数英里外的林地地表。

abstract.en: Picture ancient swamp mud that is now a black rock full of stored carbon.
abstract.cn: 想象远古沼泽的泥，如今成了蓄满碳的黑色岩石。

examples.en: Organic matter improves both the structure and the fertility of the soil.
examples.cn: 有机质既能改善土壤结构，也能提高肥力。

examples.en: The wetland stores organic matter in peat that has built up for centuries.
examples.cn: 这片湿地把有机质储存在堆积了几个世纪的泥炭里。

examples.en: Dissolved organic matter made the lake water hard to treat.
examples.cn: 溶解态有机质让湖水难以处理。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「有机 + 物质」——凡是来自活物的东西，不管是碎叶还是腐屑，都叫有机质

root: organic（希腊 organon「器官、工具」加 -ic，经拉丁 organicus）+ matter（拉丁 materia「木料、物质」，源于 mater「母亲」）；「来源于生物的物质」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses split the phrase into its soil pools, then follow the material into water and into buried rock.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把这个短语分成土壤中的几个库，然后跟着这些物质进入水体与埋藏的岩石。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: dark crumbs scattered on a seed bed, feeding worms first.
core.cn: 核心意象：撒在苗床上的深色碎屑，先喂饱蚯蚓。

branches.en: ORIGIN: it is defined by coming from life, including things still alive.
branches.cn: 来源：以来自生命来定义，包括仍然活着的部分。

branches.en: SIZE AND AGE: fragments you can see, and a dark residue you cannot.
branches.cn: 大小与年龄：看得见的碎片，与看不见的深色残余。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT: what passes a filter and what a soil test reports.
branches.cn: 计量：什么能通过滤膜，以及土壤检测报出什么。

branches.en: WATER: the same material becomes an oxygen demand figure.
branches.cn: 水：同一物质变成一项需氧量数值。

branches.en: DEEP TIME: buried and cooked into hydrocarbons.
branches.cn: 深时：被埋藏并热解成烃。

intro.en: Organic matter is made of an adjective and a noun, and both have analyzable stems with large families.
intro.cn: organic matter 由形容词与名词组成，两者都有可分析、族系庞大的词干。

latinIntro.en: Greek organon reached Latin as organicus, and materia is native Latin; the entries below record both routes, marking which one is Greek in origin.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 organon 以 organicus 进入拉丁语，materia 则是拉丁本族词；下面的词条记录两条路径，并标明哪一条源自希腊语。

items.example: Organ, organelle and organic all trace to this Greek word.
items.exampleCN: organ、organelle 与 organic 都可上溯这个希腊词。

items.example: Organic and inorganic form a matched pair.
items.exampleCN: organic 与 inorganic 构成一对。

items.example: A single organism can supply organic matter for years.
items.exampleCN: 一个生物体可以为土壤提供数年的有机质。

items.example: Inorganic matter dominates the sandy subsoil.
items.exampleCN: 砂质底土中以无机质为主。

items.example: Material and matter both descend from materia.
items.exampleCN: material 与 matter 都源自 materia。

items.example: Building material was hauled up the slope.

items.structure: matter (English noun from materia via French)
items.example: Matter can be solid, liquid or gas.
items.exampleCN: 物质可以是固体、液体或气体。

items.meaning: in a physical or significant way
items.example: The soil was materially changed by the ash.
items.exampleCN: 火山灰在实质上改变了这片土壤。

items.example: The difference is immaterial to the crop.
items.exampleCN: 这个差别对作物并无实质影响。

latinEntries.example: Latin materia meant timber before it meant subject matter.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 materia 先指木料，后来才指题材。

latinEntries.meaning: relating to an organ or instrument
latinEntries.example: Medieval Latin organicus is the adjective behind English organic.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 中世纪拉丁语 organicus 是英语 organic 背后的形容词。

definition_zh: 脆的，易碎的；脆弱的，靠不住的；（声音）尖利的
definition_en: hard but liable to break easily; fragile in temper or health; sharp and crackling in sound
core_image: 玻璃般的硬壳，一敲就裂出细纹
scene: 深秋的凉台上，老人捏着一片枯叶轻轻一折。 The dry leaf turned brittle and snapped in her fingers.
sceneCN: 这里 brittle 是「脆的、易碎的」（第 1 个义项：硬而无韧，一折即断）；句意是干枯的叶子发脆，在她指间啪地断了。

pos.zh: 脆的；易碎的；脆弱的；（声音）尖利刺耳的

derivatives.zh: 由 brittle 加 -ness 构成，义为「脆性；脆弱」
由 brittle 加 -ly 构成，义为「发脆地；尖利地（罕用）」

senses.title: Hard but easily broken
senses.definition: hard and stiff, but breaking easily under a blow or bend
senses.definitionCN: 硬而僵，但受击或弯折即碎
senses.example: The old paper was so brittle that it cracked at the fold.
senses.exampleCN: 旧纸发脆，一折就裂。
senses.why: The core image is a hard shell with no give inside.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是硬壳内里没有韧劲，一折即断。

senses.title: Easily damaged in health or temper
senses.titleCN: 脆弱的；（体质、情绪）易伤的
senses.definition: fragile, as a person's health, nerves or relationships that break under little pressure
senses.definitionCN: 健康、神经或关系稍受压力便崩溃的脆弱状态
senses.example: After the shock, his nerves grew brittle.
senses.exampleCN: 受惊之后，他的神经变得脆弱。
senses.why: What breaks at a touch in objects extends to what collapses at a touch in people.
senses.whyCN: 物一触即碎的属性，转喻为人一触即溃的状态。

senses.title: Sharp and harsh in sound or manner
senses.definition: having a sharp, crackling or coldly hard quality of sound or manner
senses.definitionCN: 声音干裂刺耳，或态度冷硬生涩
senses.example: She gave a brittle laugh and changed the subject.
senses.exampleCN: 她尖利地笑了一声，随即岔开话题。
senses.why: A brittle surface both snaps and rings; the sound sense copies that snap.
senses.whyCN: 脆物既折断又作响，声音义项模仿的就是这声脆响。

intro.en: Brittle probably grew out of an old word for breaking, related to bretan.
intro.cn: brittle 一般认为由古英语表「碎裂」的词派生而来。

items.en: brytan meant to shatter or crush to pieces.
items.cn: 古英语 brytan 意为击碎、碾碎。

items.en: britel meant liable to break, a diminutive of the breaking verb.
items.cn: 中古英语 britel 意为易碎的，由碎裂动词加指小后缀构成。

items.en: spelling settled as brittle; the word spread to temper and sound.
items.cn: 拼写定型为 brittle，词义扩展到性情与声音。

items.en: materials science fixed brittle as the technical opposite of ductile.
items.cn: 材料科学把 brittle 定为 ductile（延展性）的技术反义词。

items.en: brittle covers glass, bones, nerves and laughs.
items.cn: 如今 brittle 可形容玻璃、骨骼、神经与笑声。

note.en: Brittle sits among breaking words and stands against bendable ones.
note.cn: brittle 处于一组碎裂词之间，并与可弯折词相对。

entries.definition: short stiff hairs; to stand up in anger
entries.definitionCN: 刚毛；（毛发）竖起——只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: the quality of being brittle
entries.definitionCN: 脆性，由 brittle 派生的名词

entries.definition: a northern dialect form of brittle
entries.definitionCN: brittle 的北方方言变体

entries.definition: easily broken or damaged
entries.definitionCN: 易碎的；脆弱的，侧重需轻拿轻放

entries.definition: weak and delicate
entries.definitionCN: 虚弱纤弱的，多形容人或身体

entries.definition: firm and breaking with a clean snap
entries.definitionCN: 酥脆的，常含悦耳爽口之意

entries.definition: able to be stretched without breaking
entries.definitionCN: 有延展性的，brittle 的技术反义词

entries.definition: to break suddenly into pieces
entries.definitionCN: 粉碎；碎裂，brittle 之物的下场

normalIntro.en: Hold brittle against bristle to keep the two straight.
normalIntro.cn: 把 brittle 与 bristle 对照着记，避免混淆。

normal.en: Brittle has TT like a crack splitting the word.
normal.cn: brittle 的双写 tt 像一道裂纹把词劈开。

normal.en: Bristle is hair; brittle is glass.
normal.cn: bristle 是硬毛，brittle 是玻璃。

normal.en: Brittle bones break: the old fear of age.
normal.cn: brittle bones（脆骨）是年老的旧忧。

normal.en: Crisp snaps sweetly; brittle snaps badly.
normal.cn: crisp 脆得悦耳，brittle 脆得糟心。

normal.en: Ductile bends, brittle breaks.
normal.cn: ductile 能弯，brittle 会断。

abstract.en: Hear one dry leaf crack between two fingers.
abstract.cn: 听一片枯叶在指间断裂。

abstract.en: See the hairline zigzag run across old varnish.
abstract.cn: 看见旧漆面上细裂纹蜿蜒而过。

abstract.en: Feel a laugh with nothing warm under it.
abstract.cn: 体会笑声底下毫无暖意的感觉。

examples.en: Handle the brittle old manuscript with cotton gloves.
examples.cn: 戴棉手套翻动发脆的旧手稿。

examples.en: Their truce proved brittle and collapsed within weeks.
examples.cn: 休战证明是脆弱的，几周内便告破裂。

examples.en: He answered in a brittle voice that hid his nerves.
examples.cn: 他以尖硬的声音作答，掩饰着内心的紧张。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「玻璃透」——brittle 像「玻璃」一样硬而「透」脆，一磕就裂。

root: brittle 一般认为源自古英语 brytan（击碎），中古英语 britel 由该动词加指小后缀 -el 构成，义为「易碎的」；更早词根来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: From breaking under the hand, the word moves to breaking under stress, then to a snap in voice and manner.
sensesIntro.cn: 从手感之下的断裂，到压力之下的崩溃，再到声音态度里的干硬脆响。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hard shell cracking at the first blow.
core.cn: 核心意象：硬壳一敲即裂。

branches.en: brittle plastic
branches.cn: 脆性塑料

branches.en: brittle old bones
branches.cn: 脆弱的老年骨骼

branches.en: brittle relations
branches.cn: 脆弱的关系

branches.en: a brittle laugh
branches.cn: 尖利的笑声

branches.en: brittle and near tears
branches.cn: 强撑着几乎落泪

intro.en: Brittle is a small family: an abstract noun and a rare adverb.
intro.cn: brittle 词族很小：一个抽象名词，一个罕用副词。

latinIntro.en: The root is Germanic; its technical opposite is Latin-born ductile.
latinIntro.cn: 词根属日耳曼语族；其技术反义词 ductile 则出自拉丁语。

definition_zh: 歧视性的；区别对待的；以不公平方式按群体特征区分人的
definition_en: treating people unfairly because they belong to a particular group, or making distinctions that produce unequal treatment
core_image: 同样的岗位、同样的简历，只因姓名与口音属于某个群体就被直接刷掉，公司却拿不出与工作相关的理由
scene: 这里指「歧视性的」。 The hiring rule was discriminatory because it screened out equally qualified applicants from one group.
sceneCN: 此处指「按群体身份而非工作能力淘汰应聘者」（第 1 个义项：以不公平方式按群体特征区别对待）；句意为此项招聘规则具有歧视性，因为它把同一群体中同样合格的申请者筛掉了。可辨识物件：两摞相同的简历、面试桌、被划掉的名字、招聘公告。

pos.zh: 歧视性的；不公平区别对待的
有区分作用的（较技术化，通常用 discriminative）

senses.title: Unfair treatment by group
senses.titleCN: 按群体身份的不公平对待
senses.definition: treating people worse because of their race, sex, age, religion or other group membership rather than their individual qualities
senses.definitionCN: 因种族、性别、年龄、宗教或其他群体身份而非个人素质而给予较差待遇
senses.example: The hiring rule was discriminatory because it screened out equally qualified applicants from one group.
senses.exampleCN: 这项招聘规则具有歧视性，因为它把同一群体中同样合格的申请者筛掉了。
senses.why: Discriminatory is the adjective of discriminate, which means 'to separate, to distinguish'; when the separation is unjust, the word carries the modern condemnatory sense.
senses.whyCN: discriminatory 是 discriminate 的形容词，后者意为「分开、区分」；当这种区分不公正时，这个词就带上现代的谴责义。

senses.title: Making a distinction
senses.definition: capable of drawing a difference between things, a neutral and rather technical reading
senses.definitionCN: 能够辨别事物之间的差别，这一读法中性且偏技术化
senses.example: A discriminatory test can tell two similar alloys apart.
senses.exampleCN: 一项有区分力的测试能分辨两种相似的合金。
senses.why: The neutral sense survives in technical writing, where discrimination means accurate separation rather than prejudice.
senses.whyCN: 中性义保留在技术写作中，那里的 discrimination 指准确区分，而非偏见。

senses.title: Of a rule or policy
senses.titleCN: 政策或规则层面的歧视性
senses.definition: describing a formal rule whose effect is to exclude one group from a benefit or opportunity
senses.definitionCN: 描述某项正式规则的效果是把某一群体排除在某种利益或机会之外
senses.example: The zoning rule was discriminatory in effect even though its wording was neutral.
senses.exampleCN: 这项分区规则措辞中立，效果上却具有歧视性。
senses.why: Modern law looks at effects as well as intentions, so the adjective is applied to rules that produce exclusion indirectly.
senses.whyCN: 现代法律既看意图也看效果，因此这个形容词也用于间接造成排斥的规则。

senses.title: Of differential pricing
senses.definition: describing prices or terms set differently for groups in a way that is judged unfair
senses.definitionCN: 描述按群体设定不同价格或条件、并被判定不公的做法
senses.example: Charging the same service more in the poorer district was ruled discriminatory.
senses.exampleCN: 在较贫困地区对同一服务收取更高费用被裁定为歧视性做法。
senses.why: Price is a form of treatment, so unequal terms can be called discriminatory even without an explicit rule about identity.
senses.whyCN: 价格也是一种对待方式，因此即使没有明文身份规定，不平等的条件也可被称为歧视性。

senses.title: Of biased wording
senses.definition: describing language that assumes one group is inferior or treats it as the exception
senses.definitionCN: 描述假定某一群体低劣、或将其视为例外的语言
senses.example: The manual's discriminatory wording described female engineers as unusual.
senses.exampleCN: 这本手册的歧视性措辞把女性工程师写成不寻常的例外。
senses.why: Language carries judgments, so the adjective extends from acts to the words that shape them.
senses.whyCN: 语言带着判断，因此这个形容词从行为延伸到塑造行为的词语。

senses.title: Of hiring and admission
senses.titleCN: 招聘与录取中的歧视性
senses.definition: describing selection practices that disadvantage applicants because of group membership
senses.definitionCN: 描述因群体身份而使申请者处于不利地位的选拔做法
senses.example: The inquiry found discriminatory admission practices in three of the five colleges.
senses.exampleCN: 调查发现五所学院中有三所存在歧视性录取做法。
senses.why: Selection is where unequal treatment is most easily measured, which is why the word appears so often with hiring and admission.
senses.whyCN: 选拔最容易测量不平等待遇，因此这个词常与招聘、录取连用。

senses.title: Statistical discrimination
senses.definition: using group averages as a shortcut to judge an individual, even when the average is accurate
senses.definitionCN: 用群体平均值作为判断个人的捷径，即使该平均值本身准确
senses.example: Insurers used a discriminatory proxy when they priced policies by postcode alone.
senses.exampleCN: 保险公司仅按邮政编码定价时，使用了一个带歧视性的替代指标。
senses.why: Economics gave the word a precise reading: a group average can be true and still unjust when applied to one person.
senses.whyCN: 经济学赋予这个词精确读法：群体平均可以真实，用在个人身上仍可能不公。

senses.title: Of intent or motive
senses.definition: describing an act done because of prejudice, not merely one that happens to produce an unequal result
senses.definitionCN: 描述因偏见而实施的行为，而不只是碰巧造成不平等结果的行为
senses.example: The tribunal asked whether the remark showed discriminatory intent or mere carelessness.
senses.exampleCN: 审裁处追问那句话显示的是歧视意图，还是仅仅疏忽。
senses.why: Intent matters in law and ethics, so the adjective can qualify a motive as well as an outcome.
senses.whyCN: 意图在法律与伦理中很重要，因此这个形容词既可修饰结果，也可修饰动机。

intro.en: Discriminatory is the adjective of discriminate, from Latin discriminare 'to separate, to distinguish', built on discrimen 'a dividing line', from discernere 'to sift apart'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: discriminatory 是 discriminate 的形容词，后者来自拉丁 discriminare「分开、辨别」，其名词 discrimen 意为「分界线」，源于 discernere「筛分开」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Cernere meant 'to sift, to separate, to decide'. It supplied the core of discernere and discriminare.
items.cn: cernere 意为「筛、分开、判定」，是 discernere 与 discriminare 的核心。

items.en: Dis- 'apart' plus cernere gave discernere 'to separate, to distinguish, to perceive a difference'.
items.cn: dis-「分开」加 cernere 构成 discernere「分开、辨别、看出差别」。

items.en: Discrimen named a dividing line, a decisive moment, or a distinction between things.
items.cn: discrimen 指分界线、关键时刻或事物之间的区别。

items.en: Discriminare meant 'to divide, to distinguish, to set apart'. The English verb discriminate came from it.
items.cn: discriminare 意为「划分、辨别、使分离」，英语动词 discriminate 由此而来。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries the verb acquired the strong sense of treating a group unjustly, and the adjective followed.
items.cn: 到十九与二十世纪，这个动词获得「不公平对待某一群体」的强义，形容词也随之带上该义。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest English use of discriminatory is not precisely dated, and the deeper origin of cernere is unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：discriminatory 的最早英语用例缺乏精确年代，cernere 的更深来源亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same separating root; group two holds adjectives of unfair treatment with a different emphasis.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「分开」词根的词；第二组是侧重不同的不公平对待类形容词。

entries.definition: Can mean either to distinguish accurately or to treat a group unfairly; context decides which.
entries.definitionCN: 既可指准确辨别，也可指不公平对待群体，由语境决定。

entries.definition: The act or practice of unfair distinction, or the ability to make fine distinctions.
entries.definitionCN: 指不公平区分的做法，或精细辨别的能力。

entries.definition: Usually means showing refined judgment, as in a discriminating reader; it is not the same as discriminatory.
entries.definitionCN: 通常指有精细判断力，如「有鉴别力的读者」，与 discriminatory 不同。

entries.definition: Means serving to distinguish, a neutral technical adjective rather than a moral one.
entries.definitionCN: 意为起区分作用的，是中性技术形容词，而非道德评价。

entries.definition: Shows a preference that favours one side; it can be unconscious and need not be a formal rule.
entries.definitionCN: 显示偏袒一方，可能无意识，也不一定是正式规则。

entries.definition: Holds an opinion formed before evidence; it names an attitude more than a practice.
entries.definitionCN: 指在证据之前就形成看法，更多指态度而非做法。

entries.definition: The everyday adjective for unequal or unjust treatment; discriminatory adds the group basis.
entries.definitionCN: 指不平等或不公正对待的日常形容词；discriminatory 加上群体依据。

entries.definition: Describes rules or systems that keep people out; it stresses the effect rather than the motive.
entries.definitionCN: 描述把人挡在外的规则或制度，强调效果而非动机。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Dis- 'apart' plus cernere 'to sift': to sift apart, hence to distinguish and, unjustly, to separate people.
normal.cn: dis-「分开」加 cernere「筛」：把东西筛开，因此指辨别，也指不公正地把人分开。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: discriminatory practice, discriminatory hiring, discriminatory language.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：歧视性做法、歧视性招聘、歧视性语言。

normal.en: The family runs discriminate, discrimination, discriminating, discriminative and indiscriminate.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 discriminate、discrimination、discriminating、discriminative 与 indiscriminate。

normal.en: The neutral and the condemnatory senses sit side by side: a discriminatory test versus a discriminatory rule.
normal.cn: 中性义与谴责义并存：有区分力的测试，与歧视性的规则。

normal.en: Law looks at effects, so a neutral word can still describe a discriminatory outcome.
normal.cn: 法律看效果，因此中性的措辞仍可能描述歧视性结果。

abstract.en: Picture a sieve that keeps one kind of grain and throws the rest away.
abstract.cn: 想象一只筛子，留下一种谷粒，把其余的都扔掉。

abstract.en: Picture two identical envelopes, only one of which reaches the desk.
abstract.cn: 想象两个一模一样的信封，只有一个被送到桌上。

abstract.en: Picture a door marked neutral that only opens for certain accents.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇标着中立的门，只对某些口音打开。

examples.en: The tribunal ruled that the promotion rule was discriminatory against older staff.
examples.cn: 审裁处裁定该晋升规则对年长员工具有歧视性。

examples.en: Discriminatory pricing meant the same delivery cost more in the poorer district.
examples.cn: 歧视性定价使同一配送在较贫困地区收费更高。

examples.en: The report found no discriminatory intent, only a careless procedure.
examples.cn: 报告未发现歧视意图，只发现程序草率。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「dis（分开）+ crimin（筛选）+ atory（的）」——把人按群体筛开 → 歧视性的

root: discriminatory 是 discriminate 的形容词；discriminate 来自拉丁 discriminare「分开、辨别」，源于 discrimen「分界线」与 discernere「筛分开」，其核心为 cernere「筛、分开」。cernere 更深来源不确定，最早书证年代亦不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act of sifting: unfair group treatment, neutral distinction, exclusionary rules, differential prices, biased wording, hiring practice, statistical shortcuts and guilty intent.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次「筛分」展开：不公平的群体对待、中性的辨别、排斥性规则、差别定价、偏见措辞、招聘做法、统计捷径与有罪意图。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sieve that keeps one kind of grain and throws the rest away.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只筛子，留下一种谷粒，把其余的都扔掉。

branches.en: UNFAIR GROUP TREATMENT: the sifting is applied to people because of group membership.
branches.cn: 不公平的群体对待：筛分被用到人身上，依据是群体身份。

branches.en: NEUTRAL DISTINCTION: the same root can mean accurate separation with no moral judgment.
branches.cn: 中性辨别：同一词根也可指准确分开，不带道德判断。

branches.en: RULES AND HIRING: formal selection is where exclusion becomes measurable.
branches.cn: 规则与招聘：正式选拔是排斥最容易被测量的地方。

branches.en: PRICE AND WORDING: unequal terms and biased language are quieter forms of the same sieve.
branches.cn: 价格与措辞：不平等条件与偏见语言是同一只筛子更安静的形式。

branches.en: AVERAGES AND INTENT: a true group average can still misjudge a person, and motive decides blame.
branches.cn: 平均值与意图：真实的群体平均仍可能误判个人，而动机决定责任。

intro.en: The adjective is built on a Latin verb of separating, and its derived forms keep the neutral and the condemnatory readings side by side.
intro.cn: 这个形容词建立在拉丁「分开」动词上，其派生形式同时保留中性义与谴责义。

latinIntro.en: Latin cernere, discernere and discriminare supply the root; English added discriminate, discrimination and the negative forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 cernere、discernere 与 discriminare 提供词根；英语又造出 discriminate、discrimination 与否定形式。

items.example: The prefix separates the sieve from the grain.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把筛子与谷粒分开。

items.example: The root carries the image of sifting.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着筛分的意象。

items.meaning: to distinguish or to treat unequally
items.example: The verb can be neutral or damning.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词可以是中性，也可以是谴责。

items.meaning: the act of distinguishing or unfair treatment

derivatives.meaning: unfair distinction or the act of distinguishing

latinEntries.meaning: to sift, to separate, to decide

definition_zh: 空气压力；气压（可指大气压，也常指轮胎、气球等密闭空间内的气压）
definition_en: the pressure exerted by air, either by the atmosphere or by air enclosed in a space such as a tyre or a balloon
core_image: 一只轮胎被气泵充得鼓起，胎壁绷紧，手指按下去很硬
scene: 修车铺里，技师把气枪接到轮胎气门，表盘上的指针慢慢抬起。 He checked the air pressure in all four tyres before the drive.
sceneCN: 这里 air pressure 指「密闭空间内空气的压强」（第 3 个义项：轮胎等密闭空间的气压）；句意为他在出发前检查了四条轮胎的气压。图中可辨识物件：气泵、气枪、轮胎气门、压力表。

pos.zh: 空气压力；气压（不可数名词）

forms.label: 复数（不同空间或行星的气压）

senses.title: Pressure exerted by air
senses.definition: the pressure that air exerts on the surfaces it touches
senses.definitionCN: 空气对它所接触的表面施加的压强
senses.example: Air pressure kept the suction cup against the glass.
senses.exampleCN: 空气压使吸盘贴在玻璃上。
senses.why: the phrase is the plainest name for the force air applies, whether enclosed or open.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法是空气所施力最朴素的名字，无论密闭还是敞开。

senses.title: The atmosphere's pressure
senses.definition: the pressure of the open atmosphere, the everyday name for atmospheric pressure
senses.definitionCN: 开阔大气的压强，即大气压的日常说法
senses.example: Air pressure fell sharply before the storm arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴来临前气压急剧下降。
senses.why: weather talk prefers the short phrase, while scientific writing uses the longer one.
senses.whyCN: 谈天气偏爱短说法，科学写作则用更长的正式说法。

senses.title: Pressure inside a tyre or ball
senses.definition: the pressure of air enclosed in a tyre, balloon or ball
senses.definitionCN: 封闭在轮胎、气球或球内的空气压强
senses.example: He checked the air pressure in all four tyres before the drive.
senses.exampleCN: 他在出发前检查了四条轮胎的气压。
senses.why: an enclosed space makes the phrase countable in practice: each tyre has its own pressure.
senses.whyCN: 密闭空间使这个说法在实际中可数：每条轮胎都有自己的气压。

senses.title: Working pressure in pneumatics
senses.definition: the pressure at which compressed air operates tools and machinery
senses.definitionCN: 压缩空气驱动工具与机械时的工作压强
senses.example: The workshop runs its tools at six bar of air pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 这个车间以六巴的气压驱动工具。
senses.why: industry needs a controlled supply, and the phrase names the working value.
senses.whyCN: 工业需要受控的气源，这个说法就指工作数值。

senses.title: Pressure in ducts and cabins
senses.definition: the pressure of moving or conditioned air inside ducts, cabins and buildings
senses.definitionCN: 风道、客舱与建筑内部流动或调节空气的压强
senses.example: Cabin air pressure is kept close to the value at a moderate altitude.
senses.exampleCN: 客舱气压保持在中等海拔的数值附近。
senses.why: ventilation and flight both manage air as a working medium, and pressure is the variable they control.
senses.whyCN: 通风与飞行都把空气当工作介质，压强就是它们控制的变量。

senses.title: Sound pressure
senses.definition: the tiny rapid variations in air pressure that carry sound
senses.definitionCN: 携带声音的空气压强的微小快速变化
senses.example: A loudspeaker produces sound by making rapid air pressure changes.
senses.exampleCN: 扬声器靠制造快速的空气压强变化来发声。
senses.why: sound is a wave of pressure, so acoustics borrowed the everyday phrase for a precise quantity.
senses.whyCN: 声音是一种压强波，声学便借用这个日常说法来指一个精确量。

senses.title: Wind pressure on structures
senses.definition: the force that moving air exerts on a building, bridge or tower
senses.definitionCN: 流动空气对建筑、桥梁或塔施加的力
senses.example: Engineers tested the tower against extreme wind pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师测试这座塔能否承受极端风压。
senses.why: wind is moving air, and its push on a surface is measured as pressure.
senses.whyCN: 风是流动的空气，它对表面的推挤以压强来计量。

senses.title: Pressure changes and the body
senses.definition: the effects of changing air pressure on ears, lungs and blood at altitude or underwater
senses.definitionCN: 在高原或水下，气压变化对耳、肺与血液的影响
senses.example: The descent made the air pressure change faster than her ears could equalise.
senses.exampleCN: 下潜时气压变化太快，她的耳朵来不及平衡。
senses.why: the body is a pressure vessel too, so physiology uses the same phrase.
senses.whyCN: 人体也是一个压力容器，因此生理学使用同一个说法。

intro.en: Air pressure joins the old Germanic word air, borrowed through Latin and Greek, with Latin-based pressure. The compound belongs to the scientific English of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.
intro.cn: air pressure 把经拉丁语与希腊语借入的古日耳曼词 air 与拉丁来源的 pressure 组合起来，这一复合说法属于十七、十八世纪的科学英语。

items.en: Greek aēr meant 'lower air, mist', as opposed to aithēr, the bright upper layer. Its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 希腊 aēr 指「低层空气、雾」，与指明亮上层的 aithēr 相对。其更深来源不确定。

items.en: Latin aer and Old French air carried the word into English, where it replaced older native terms for the lower atmosphere.
items.cn: 拉丁 aer 与古法语 air 把这个词带入英语，取代了较早表示低层大气的本族词。

items.en: Pressure comes from Latin pressura 'a pressing', from premere 'to press'.
items.cn: pressure 来自拉丁 pressura「压、挤压」，出自 premere「压」。

items.en: Once the barometer showed that air has weight, air pressure became a fixed phrase in experimental writing.
items.cn: 一旦气压计表明空气有重量，air pressure 就成了实验写作中的固定说法。

items.en: In later use the phrase spread to tyres, balloons and pneumatic tools, where the air is enclosed rather than atmospheric.
items.cn: 在后来的用法中，这个说法扩展到轮胎、气球与气动工具，那里的空气是封闭的而非大气的。

items.en: Source uncertain (origin of aēr and first date): the pre-Greek source of aēr is not established, and the first English use of the compound is not exactly dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（aēr 的来源与首见年代）：aēr 在希腊语之前的来源未得到证明，这一复合说法在英语中的首见也没有确切年代。

note.en: Group one holds closely related phrases that name a different thing; group two holds the real alternatives for the same pressure.
note.cn: 第一组是关系密切、却指另一事物的说法；第二组才是同一种压强的真正替代说法。

entries.definition: The hyphenated form used before a noun, as in air-pressure gauge; it is the same quantity as a modifier.
entries.definitionCN: 放在名词前时加连字符的形式，如气压表；仍是同一个量充当修饰语。

entries.definition: A machine that raises air pressure; it produces the quantity rather than being it.
entries.definitionCN: 提高空气压强的机器；它产生这个量，而不是这个量本身。

entries.definition: A local region of different air, often felt in flight; it names a place, not a pressure value.
entries.definitionCN: 一块空气状况不同的局部区域，飞行中常有感觉；指位置，不指压强数值。

entries.definition: The movement of air; it describes motion, while air pressure describes push.
entries.definitionCN: 空气的流动；描述运动，而 air pressure 描述推力。

entries.definition: The formal name for the open atmosphere's pressure; air pressure is its everyday and broader counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 开阔大气压强的正式名称；air pressure 是其日常且范围更宽的对应说法。

entries.definition: The pressure inside a tyre; it is the commonest everyday use of air pressure.
entries.definitionCN: 轮胎内部的压强；是 air pressure 最常见的日常用法。

entries.definition: Pressure as read by a barometer; common in weather reports.
entries.definitionCN: 气压计读出的压强；常见于天气报告。

entries.definition: The controlled pressure inside an aircraft cabin; a specialised case of enclosed air pressure.
entries.definitionCN: 飞机客舱内受控的压强；是密闭空气压强的一个专门情形。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real word parts, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: air plus pressure: the push that air itself exerts.
normal.cn: air 加 pressure：空气本身施加的推挤。

normal.en: The family runs air, air pressure, atmospheric pressure, pressurize.
normal.cn: 同族说法包括 air、air pressure、atmospheric pressure、pressurize。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the enclosures: tyre pressure, cabin pressure, air-pressure gauge.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出密闭场合：轮胎气压、客舱气压、气压表。

normal.en: Weather talk uses the short phrase; scientific writing prefers atmospheric pressure.
normal.cn: 谈天气用短说法，科学写作更爱用 atmospheric pressure。

normal.en: Sound is a rapid series of air pressure changes.
normal.cn: 声音是一连串快速的空气压强变化。

abstract.en: Picture a tyre swelling until the wall feels hard under a thumb.
abstract.cn: 想象轮胎鼓起，直到拇指按上去胎壁发硬。

abstract.en: Picture a suction cup staying on glass because the air outside keeps pushing.
abstract.cn: 想象吸盘贴在玻璃上，因为外面的空气一直在推。

abstract.en: Picture a sound wave as a ripple of squeezed air moving toward an ear.
abstract.cn: 想象声波是一圈被挤压的空气向耳朵推进。

examples.en: Check the air pressure before a long drive.
examples.cn: 长途驾驶前先检查气压。

examples.en: Air pressure in the cabin is kept near a moderate altitude value.
examples.cn: 客舱气压保持在接近中等海拔的数值。

examples.en: A sudden change in air pressure can make ears ache.
examples.cn: 气压骤变会让人耳朵疼。

root: 希腊 aēr「低层空气、雾」→ 拉丁 aer → 古法语 air → 英语 air；拉丁 premere「压」→ pressura → pressure；组合为 air pressure。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one plain phrase: air pushing on a surface, the open atmosphere, a tyre's enclosed air, pneumatic tools, ducts and cabins, sound waves, wind on buildings and the body's own pressure balance.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个朴素说法展开：空气推压表面、开阔大气、轮胎内的封闭空气、气动工具、风道与客舱、声波、建筑所受的风压，以及人体的压力平衡。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tyre swelling until its wall feels hard under a thumb.
core.cn: 核心意象：轮胎鼓起，直到拇指按上去胎壁发硬。

branches.en: THE OPEN AIR: the plain push of air, and the atmosphere's own pressure.
branches.cn: 开阔空气：空气朴素的推力，以及大气本身的压强。

branches.en: ENCLOSED SPACES: tyres and cabins each hold their own pressure.
branches.cn: 密闭空间：轮胎与客舱各自持有一份压强。

branches.en: WORKING AIR: compressed air drives tools at a chosen value.
branches.cn: 工作空气：压缩空气以选定数值驱动工具。

branches.en: AIR IN MOTION: sound is a pressure ripple, and wind is a pressure load.
branches.cn: 运动空气：声是压强的涟漪，风是压强的载荷。

branches.en: THE BODY: ears and lungs must equalise what the air does.
branches.cn: 身体：耳与肺必须平衡空气造成的变化。

intro.en: Air pressure is a compound of a native English noun and a Latin borrowing, so its two halves belong to different layers of the vocabulary.
intro.cn: air pressure 是一个英语本族名词与一个拉丁借词的复合，两半属于词汇的不同层次。

latinIntro.en: Greek aēr passed through Latin aer into English air, while Latin premere and pressura supply pressure.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 aēr 经拉丁 aer 进入英语 air，而拉丁 premere 与 pressura 提供 pressure。

definition_zh: 移民入境；（总称）入境移民；入境查验
definition_en: the act or process of coming to a country in order to live there, or the flow of people who do so

scene: 海关大厅里，一家人提着行李箱排在队伍末端，孩子紧紧抓着护照。 Immigration has reshaped the neighbourhood's shops and schools.
sceneCN: 这里 immigration 指「人口迁入一个国家并定居的过程」（第 1 个义项：入境定居这一行为）；句意为移民入境改变了这个街区的店铺与学校。图中可辨识物件：到达口长队、贴标签的行李箱、护照、接机的人群。

pos.zh: 移民入境；入境移民（不可数；指具体批次时可作可数）

senses.title: The act of settling in a new country
senses.titleCN: 迁入他国并定居的行为
senses.definition: the act of coming to a country that is not one's own in order to live there
senses.definitionCN: 来到并非自己所属的国家并在此生活的行为
senses.example: Immigration has reshaped the neighbourhood's shops and schools.
senses.exampleCN: 移民入境改变了这个街区的店铺与学校。
senses.why: the prefix means into and the root means to move, so immigration is movement inward, seen from the receiving country.
senses.whyCN: 前缀意为「进入」，词根意为「迁移」，因此 immigration 是从接收国角度看到的向内移动。

senses.title: The volume of people arriving
senses.titleCN: 入境移民的总量与流量
senses.definition: the number or flow of people entering a country over a period
senses.definitionCN: 一段时间内进入一国的人数或人流
senses.example: Immigration doubled in the decade after the mines opened.
senses.exampleCN: 矿区开工后的十年里，入境移民数量翻了一番。
senses.why: an uncountable noun easily turns into a quantity word, as with traffic or rainfall.
senses.whyCN: 不可数名词很容易转为数量词，就像「交通量」或「降雨量」那样。

senses.title: The border admission process
senses.definition: the official procedure by which a country admits or refuses entrants
senses.definitionCN: 一国准许或拒绝入境者的官方程序
senses.example: The queue at immigration stretched past the baggage hall.
senses.exampleCN: 入境查验的队伍一直排到行李厅之外。
senses.why: the abstract noun metonymically names the desk and the officers that carry the process out.
senses.whyCN: 抽象名词以转喻方式指执行这一程序的服务台与官员。

senses.title: Immigrants taken as a group
senses.definition: the people who have entered a country, considered collectively
senses.definitionCN: 已经进入一国的人，作为整体来看
senses.example: Immigration built the city's garment trade in two generations.
senses.exampleCN: 入境移民在两代人之内建起了这座城市的制衣业。
senses.why: the act stands for the actors, a common shortcut in political speech.
senses.whyCN: 用行为指代行为者，是政治语言中常见的省略。

senses.title: A component of population change
senses.definition: the gain of people from abroad in the accounting of a population
senses.definitionCN: 在人口核算中来自国外的净增人数
senses.example: Natural increase fell, so immigration kept the population growing.
senses.exampleCN: 自然增长下降，因此移民入境维持了人口增长。
senses.why: demographers balance births, deaths, immigration and emigration, and each one is a line in the ledger.
senses.whyCN: 人口学者在出生、死亡、迁入与迁出之间做平衡，每一项都是账簿上的一行。

senses.title: Colonization by a species
senses.definition: the arrival of organisms into a habitat where they were not previously established
senses.definitionCN: 生物进入此前并未立足的栖息地
senses.example: Immigration of new species followed the opening of the canal.
senses.exampleCN: 运河开通之后，新物种随之迁入。
senses.why: ecology borrows the word because individuals arriving and settling is the same pattern at a different scale.
senses.whyCN: 生态学借用这个词，因为个体到来并定居，是同一格局在不同尺度上的表现。

senses.title: A historical wave or era
senses.titleCN: 历史上的移民潮与时代
senses.definition: a distinct period or wave in which large numbers of people entered a country
senses.definitionCN: 大批人口进入某国的特定时期或浪潮
senses.example: The great immigration of the 1880s left its mark on the census.
senses.exampleCN: 19 世纪 80 年代的移民大潮在普查中留下了印记。
senses.why: historians turn the process into a countable event when a wave has a clear beginning and end.
senses.whyCN: 当一次浪潮起止清楚时，历史学者会把这一过程变成可计数的事件。

senses.title: A political issue
senses.titleCN: 作为政治议题的移民问题
senses.definition: the framing of entry and settlement as a matter of public dispute and policy
senses.definitionCN: 把入境与定居框定为公共争论与政策问题
senses.example: Immigration dominated the debate in every constituency.
senses.exampleCN: 移民问题在每一个选区都主导了辩论。
senses.why: once the word becomes a topic rather than an event, it can dominate an election without naming any person.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词成为议题而非事件，它就能在未指名任何人的情况下主导一场选举。

intro.en: Immigration rests on Latin immigrare 'to move into', from in- 'into' plus migrare 'to depart, migrate'. The English noun appeared in the seventeenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: immigration 源于拉丁 immigrare「迁入」，由 in-「进入」与 migrare「离开、迁移」构成。英语名词出现于 17 世纪。年代均为约数。

items.en: Migrare meant 'to move from one place to another, to change residence'. Its own earlier origin is not established, and the Indo-European root sometimes proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: migrare 意为「从一处移到另一处、更换居所」。它更早的来源未得到证明，常为其提出的印欧词根属重构形式。

items.en: The preposition in 'into' became a prefix marking motion inward, the mirror of e- or ex- marking motion out.
items.cn: 介词 in「进入」成为前缀，标记向内的移动，与标记向外移动的 e- 或 ex- 正相对。

items.en: In- plus migrare gave immigrare 'to move into a place, to settle there', used of people and later of animals.
items.cn: in- 加 migrare 构成 immigrare「迁入某地并定居」，用于人，后来也用于动物。

items.en: English formed immigration from the stem of immigrate in the seventeenth century, at first for settlement within a country as well as across borders.
items.cn: 英语在 17 世纪用 immigrate 的词干构成 immigration，最初既指跨国入境，也指一国之内的迁居。

items.en: Border controls and mass shipping in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries narrowed the word to entry into a state, and made it a standard term of policy and demography.
items.cn: 19 与 20 世纪的边境管控与大规模航运，把这个词收窄为进入国家，并使其成为政策与人口学的标准术语。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Latin history of migrare is unsettled, and the earliest English citation of the noun is not precisely fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：migrare 在拉丁语之前的历史尚无定论，这个名词的最早英语书证也没有精确年代。

note.en: Group one holds the near-identical migration words that differ only by direction; group two holds words for arrival and settlement.
note.cn: 第一组是只差方向的迁移类近形词；第二组是表示到来与定居的说法。

entries.definition: The same movement seen from the country people leave, with e- 'out' instead of in- 'into'.
entries.definitionCN: 同一移动从人们离开的国家看，前缀为「向外」而非「向内」。

entries.definition: Movement from one place to another without specifying whether a border is crossed; it covers birds, workers and data.
entries.definitionCN: 从一地到另一地的移动，不说明是否越过国境；可指鸟类、劳动者与数据。

entries.definition: The person who immigrates; the noun of action and the noun of person are constantly swapped in speech.
entries.definitionCN: 迁入的人；表动作的名词与表人的名词在口语中常被互换。

entries.definition: The person who emigrates, named from the sending side; the same individual can be both terms at once.
entries.definitionCN: 迁出的人，从输出方命名；同一个人可以同时是两个称呼。

entries.definition: A mass arrival of people, money or things; it stresses volume and suddenness rather than the legal act.
entries.definitionCN: 人、钱或物的大量涌入；强调数量与突然性，而非法律行为。

entries.definition: The process of making a permanent home in a new place; it can follow immigration but is not the crossing itself.
entries.definitionCN: 在新地方安家的过程；可以发生在移民之后，但不等于越境本身。

entries.definition: The instant of reaching a place; it says nothing about staying or about official permission.
entries.definitionCN: 到达某地的那一刻；不涉及是否留下或是否获准。

entries.definition: A planned move to a new place, often arranged by authorities for refugees; it is a policy channel of immigration.
entries.definitionCN: 有计划的迁往新地，常由当局为难民安排；是移民入境的一种政策渠道。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real prefix, the real root and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的前缀、真实的词根与真实的固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The prefix means into and the root means move: movement inward.
normal.cn: 前缀意为进入，词根意为迁移：向内的移动。

normal.en: The pair immigration and emigration differ only in the direction of the prefix.
normal.cn: 移民入境与移民出境这一对词，只差前缀的方向。

normal.en: The person noun adds a ending for the one who does it.
normal.cn: 表人的名词加一个表施动者的词尾，指做这件事的人。

normal.en: Fixed phrases such as immigration policy and immigration control belong to the border sense.
normal.cn: 移民政策、入境管控这类固定搭配属于边境义。

normal.en: In demography it is one line in the ledger beside births and deaths.
normal.cn: 在人口学中，它是出生与死亡旁边账簿上的一行。

abstract.en: Picture a one-way door that only opens from the outside.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇单向门，只能从外面推开。

abstract.en: Picture a river splitting into two channels, one called in and one called out.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河分成两条水道，一条叫进，一条叫出。

abstract.en: Picture a household ledger where one column is arrivals and the opposite column departures.
abstract.cn: 想象一本家庭账簿，一栏记到来，对面一栏记离开。

examples.en: Immigration rose sharply after the labour shortage of the 1950s.
examples.cn: 20 世纪 50 年代劳动力短缺之后，移民入境急剧上升。

examples.en: The ministry published immigration figures for the first quarter.
examples.cn: 该部门公布了第一季度的移民入境数字。

examples.en: Students queued at immigration for nearly two hours.
examples.cn: 学生们在入境查验处排了近两个小时的队。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一民·进来」——一批人进来定居，就是移民入境

root: 拉丁 in-「进入」+ migrare「迁移」→ immigrare「迁入定居」；英语 immigration 于 17 世纪由 immigrate 的词干构成。migrare 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement seen from the receiving side: the act of entry, the volume of arrivals, the desk that checks them, the people themselves, the line in the population ledger, the arrival of a species, a historical wave and a political issue.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从接收方看到的同一次移动展开：入境的行为、到来者的总量、查验的服务台、这些人本身、人口账簿上的一行、物种的到来、历史浪潮与政治议题。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a queue at an arrival gate, each suitcase carrying a life that is about to be unpacked somewhere else.
core.cn: 核心意象：到达口的一条长队，每只行李箱里都装着一段即将在别处展开的生活。

branches.en: CROSSING: the base act of coming in order to stay.
branches.cn: 越境而入：为了留下而进来的基础行为。

branches.en: VOLUME AND WAVE: the flow can be counted, and a counted flow becomes a historical wave.
branches.cn: 总量与浪潮：流量可以被计数，而被计数的流量会成为历史浪潮。

branches.en: CHECKPOINT: the abstract noun stands for the desk and the officers who carry the process out.
branches.cn: 查验口：抽象名词指执行该程序的服务台与官员。

branches.en: THE ARRIVING: people taken as a group, and, in ecology, organisms colonizing a habitat.
branches.cn: 到来者：作为整体的人，以及在生态学中定殖栖息的生物。

branches.en: LEDGER AND DEBATE: one line in population accounting, and one topic in public argument.
branches.cn: 账簿与争论：人口核算中的一行，也是公共争论中的一个议题。

intro.en: Immigration is a prefix, a root and a suffix, and the same pieces build the whole migration family.
intro.cn: immigration 由一个前缀、一个词根与一个后缀构成，同样的成分也构成整个迁移词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin in- marks motion inward, migrare supplies the root of moving, and -ation turns the verb into an action noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 in- 标记向内移动，migrare 提供「迁移」的词根，-ation 把动词变成表动作的名词。

items.example: The prefix directs the movement toward the receiving country.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把移动朝向接收国。

items.meaning: move from one place to another
items.example: The root supplies the idea of changing residence.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供更换居所的意思。
她的祖父母在 20 世纪 30 年代迁入。

items.example: It builds the person noun from the verb.
items.exampleCN: 它由动词构成表人的名词。

items.meaning: a person who moves into a country
items.example: The first immigrant on the list arrived in 1848.
items.exampleCN: 名单上的第一位移民于 1848 年抵达。

items.example: It turns the verb into the name of the process.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成过程之名。

items.meaning: the process of moving into a country
items.example: Immigration filled the mills with new workers.
items.exampleCN: 移民入境为工厂填满了新工人。

items.example: The opposite prefix names the same movement from the other end.
items.exampleCN: 相反的前缀从另一端为同一移动命名。

items.meaning: to move out of a country
items.example: The family emigrated in search of work.
items.exampleCN: 这家人为寻找工作而迁出。
